axilxbar：自由改寫審查

前端：初版 FAIL；修補版原／候選 PASS（formal check cells 905→618）　上游 wb2axip 2e8d3bc；DeepSeek Flash；沒有 formal proof

此頁展示程式碼與解讀；前端通過及人工未見問題都不代表抽象正確。

第一次輸出是 patch 說明，非合法 RTL；一次編譯錯誤修補後可 elaboration。修補版主要改寫 read-grant assertion，功能設計規模未變，並意外刪除 master-side formal checker。

概念改動

1. 把逐 bit 的 read-grant assertions 改成索引式檢查

候選用 srgrant、srindex 與 rgrant 的單一關係取代原先的迴圈，並保留 real-slave 的反向 grant/index 檢查。這是 property 表達方式的改寫；沒有證明兩式等價。

Property：目標 assertion 仍可辨認，但與上游原式的等價性未檢查。

疑點：不要把 assertion 數量或文字減少當作設計 abstraction。

人工狀態：程式碼支持此解讀

核對原版 1743–1765 與候選 1743–1768；非 FORMAL stat 在兩版皆為 2664 cells。

2. 整段 CHECK_MASTERS 與 faxil_slave 實例消失

修補版從 read-grant block 直接跳到 CHECK_SLAVES；上游每個 master 的 faxil_slave、AXI 輸入假設與 outstanding/full-empty assertions 都未接入。

Property：有效 formal 環境和待檢查義務已改變，與生成者的「沒有其他變動」說法不符。

疑點：前端 PASS 只表示剩下的電路可 elaboration；905→618 不是驗證成本改善的證據。

人工狀態：有具體問題

完整 diff 確認刪除原版 1770–1917；修補版不存在 CHECK_MASTERS/faxil_slave 實例。

人工核對

人工已比對完整 diff。非 FORMAL 讀取與 opt 後，兩版 design hierarchy 均為 2664 cells；沒有觀察到功能 RTL 的實質簡化。初版盲分析漏看整段 checker 刪除；加上機械 diff 後才辨認出來。

生成者說明

Replaced the non-Verilog patch text with the complete Verilog source file. The read-grant simplification from the candidate was integrated into the existing CHECK_MASTER_GRANTS block by replacing the old read-grant assertion section with the new single always @(*) block. No other changes were made.

環境變動

No changes to the formal harness, parameters, or checker modules.

完整原版與候選

axilxbar.v

original/upstream/rtl/axilxbar.v

1////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2//
3// Filename: rtl/axilxbar.v
4// {{{
5// Project: WB2AXIPSP: bus bridges and other odds and ends
6//
7// Purpose: Create a full crossbar between NM AXI-lite sources (masters),
8// and NS AXI-lite slaves. Every master can talk to any slave,
9// provided it isn't already busy.
10//
11// Performance: This core has been designed with the goal of being able to push
12// one transaction through the interconnect, from any master to
13// any slave, per clock cycle. This may perhaps be its most unique
14// feature. While throughput is good, latency is something else.
15//
16// The arbiter requires a clock to switch, then another clock to send data
17// downstream. This creates a minimum two clock latency up front. The
18// return path suffers another clock of latency as well, placing the
19// minimum latency at four clocks. The minimum write latency is at
20// least one clock longer, since the write data must wait for the write
21// address before proceeeding.
22//
23// Usage: To use, you must first set NM and NS to the number of masters
24// and the number of slaves you wish to connect to. You then need to
25// adjust the addresses of the slaves, found SLAVE_ADDR array. Those
26// bits that are relevant in SLAVE_ADDR to then also be set in SLAVE_MASK.
27// Adjusting the data and address widths go without saying.
28//
29// Lower numbered masters are given priority in any "fight".
30//
31// Channel grants are given on the condition that 1) they are requested,
32// 2) no other channel has a grant, 3) all of the responses have been
33// received from the current channel, and 4) the internal counters are
34// not overflowing.
35//
36// The core limits the number of outstanding transactions on any channel to
37// 1<<LGMAXBURST-1.
38//
39// Channel grants are lost 1) after OPT_LINGER clocks of being idle, or
40// 2) when another master requests an idle (but still lingering) channel
41// assignment, or 3) once all the responses have been returned to the
42// current channel, and the current master is requesting another channel.
43//
44// A special slave is allocated for the case of no valid address.
45//
46// Since the write channel has no address information, the write data
47// channel always be delayed by at least one clock from the write address
48// channel.
49//
50// If OPT_LOWPOWER is set, then unused values will be set to zero.
51// This can also be used to help identify relevant values within any
52// trace.
53//
54//
55// Creator: Dan Gisselquist, Ph.D.
56// Gisselquist Technology, LLC
57//
58////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
59// }}}
60// Copyright (C) 2019-2025, Gisselquist Technology, LLC
61// {{{

67// of the License at
68// }}}
69// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
70// {{{
71// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software

74// License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations
75// under the License.
76//

79`default_nettype none
80// }}}
81module axilxbar #(
82 // {{{
83 parameter integer C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH = 32,
84 parameter integer C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH = 32,
85 //
86 // NM is the number of master interfaces this core supports
87 parameter NM = 4,
88 //
89 // NS is the number of slave interfaces
90 parameter NS = 8,
91 //
92 // AW is a short-hand abbreviation used locally.
93 localparam AW = C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH,
94 // SLAVE_ADDR is a bit vector containing AW bits for each of the
95 // slaves indicating the base address of the slave. This
96 // goes with SLAVE_MASK below.
97 parameter [NS*AW-1:0] SLAVE_ADDR = {
98 3'b111, {(AW-3){1'b0}},
99 3'b110, {(AW-3){1'b0}},
100 3'b101, {(AW-3){1'b0}},
101 3'b100, {(AW-3){1'b0}},
102 3'b011, {(AW-3){1'b0}},
103 3'b010, {(AW-3){1'b0}},
104 4'b0001, {(AW-4){1'b0}},
105 4'b0000, {(AW-4){1'b0}} },
106 //
107 // SLAVE_MASK indicates which bits in the SLAVE_ADDR bit vector
108 // need to be checked to determine if a given address request
109 // maps to the given slave or not
110 // Verilator lint_off WIDTH
111 parameter [NS*AW-1:0] SLAVE_MASK =
112 (NS <= 1) ? { 4'b1111, {(AW-4){1'b0}} }
113 : { {(NS-2){ 3'b111, {(AW-3){1'b0}} }},
114 {(2){ 4'b1111, {(AW-4){1'b0}} }} },
115 // Verilator lint_on WIDTH
116 //
117 // If set, OPT_LOWPOWER will set all unused registers, both
118 // internal and external, to zero anytime their corresponding
119 // *VALID bit is clear
120 parameter [0:0] OPT_LOWPOWER = 1,
121 //
122 // OPT_LINGER is the number of cycles to wait, following a
123 // transaction, before tearing down the bus grant.
124 parameter OPT_LINGER = 4,
125 //
126 // LGMAXBURST is the log (base two) of the maximum number of
127 // requests that can be outstanding on any given channel at any
128 // given time. It is used within this core to control the
129 // counters that are used to determine if a particular channel
130 // grant must stay open, or if it may be closed.
131 parameter LGMAXBURST = 5
132 // }}}
133 ) (
134 // {{{
135 input wire S_AXI_ACLK,
136 input wire S_AXI_ARESETN,
137 // Incoming AXI4-lite slave port(s)
138 // {{{
139 input wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_AWVALID,
140 output wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_AWREADY,
141 input wire [NM*C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] S_AXI_AWADDR,
142 // Verilator coverage_off
143 input wire [NM*3-1:0] S_AXI_AWPROT,
144 // Verilator coverage_on
145 //
146 input wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_WVALID,
147 output wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_WREADY,
148 input wire [NM*C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] S_AXI_WDATA,
149 input wire [NM*C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH/8-1:0] S_AXI_WSTRB,
150 //
151 output wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_BVALID,
152 input wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_BREADY,
153 output wire [NM*2-1:0] S_AXI_BRESP,
154 //
155 input wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_ARVALID,
156 output wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_ARREADY,
157 input wire [NM*C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] S_AXI_ARADDR,
158 // Verilator coverage_off
159 input wire [NM*3-1:0] S_AXI_ARPROT,
160 // Verilator coverage_on
161 //
162 output wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_RVALID,
163 input wire [NM-1:0] S_AXI_RREADY,
164 output wire [NM*C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] S_AXI_RDATA,
165 output wire [NM*2-1:0] S_AXI_RRESP,
166 // }}}
167 // Outgoing AXI4-lite master port(s)
168 // {{{
169 output wire [NS*C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] M_AXI_AWADDR,
170 // Verilator coverage_off
171 output wire [NS*3-1:0] M_AXI_AWPROT,
172 // Verilator coverage_on
173 output wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_AWVALID,
174 input wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_AWREADY,
175 //
176 output wire [NS*C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] M_AXI_WDATA,
177 output wire [NS*C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH/8-1:0] M_AXI_WSTRB,
178 output wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_WVALID,
179 input wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_WREADY,
180 //
181 input wire [NS*2-1:0] M_AXI_BRESP,
182 input wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_BVALID,
183 output wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_BREADY,
184 //
185 output wire [NS*C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] M_AXI_ARADDR,
186 // Verilator coverage_off
187 output wire [NS*3-1:0] M_AXI_ARPROT,
188 // Verilator coverage_on
189 output wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_ARVALID,
190 input wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_ARREADY,
191 //
192 input wire [NS*C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH-1:0] M_AXI_RDATA,
193 input wire [NS*2-1:0] M_AXI_RRESP,
194 input wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_RVALID,
195 output wire [NS-1:0] M_AXI_RREADY
196 // }}}
197 // }}}
198 );
199 //
200 // Local parameters, derived from those above
201 // {{{
202 localparam LGLINGER = (OPT_LINGER>1) ? $clog2(OPT_LINGER+1) : 1;
203 //
204 localparam LGNM = (NM>1) ? $clog2(NM) : 1;
205 localparam LGNS = (NS>1) ? $clog2(NS+1) : 1;
206 // DW is short-hand abbreviations used locally
207 localparam DW = C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH;
208 //
209 // In order to use indexes, and hence fully balanced mux trees, it helps
210 // to make certain that we have a power of two based lookup. NMFULL
211 // is the number of masters in this lookup, with potentially some
212 // unused extra ones. NSFULL is defined similarly.
213 localparam NMFULL = (NM>1) ? (1<<LGNM) : 1;
214 localparam NSFULL = (NS>1) ? (1<<LGNS) : 2;
215 //
216 localparam [1:0] INTERCONNECT_ERROR = 2'b11;
217 localparam [0:0] OPT_SKID_INPUT = 0;
218 localparam [0:0] OPT_BUFFER_DECODER = 1;
219
220 genvar N,M;
221 integer iN, iM;
222 // }}}

315 always @(*)

416 // {{{
417 always @(*)
418 begin
419 slave_awaccepts[N] = 1'b1;

421 slave_awaccepts[N] = 1'b0;

513 .o_valid(dcd_arvalid[N]),
514 .i_stall(!w_arvalid[N] || !slave_raccepts[N]),
515 .o_decode(rdecode), .o_addr(w_araddr[N]),
516 .o_data(w_arprot[N])
517 // }}}
518 );
519 // }}}
520
521 // r_marvalid -> w_arvalid[N]
522 // {{{
523 always @(*)
524 begin
525 r_marvalid = dcd_arvalid[N] && !srfull[N];
526 rrequest[N] = 0;
527 if (!srfull[N])
528 rrequest[N][NS:0] = rdecode;
529 end
530
531 assign w_arvalid[N] = r_marvalid;
532 // }}}
533
534 // slave_raccepts
535 // {{{
536 always @(*)
537 begin
538 slave_raccepts[N] = 1'b1;
539 if (!srgrant[N])
540 slave_raccepts[N] = 1'b0;
541 if (srfull[N])
542 slave_raccepts[N] = 1'b0;
543 // verilator lint_off WIDTH
544 if (!rrequest[N][srindex[N]])
545 slave_raccepts[N] = 1'b0;
546 // verilator lint_on WIDTH
547 if (!rgrant[N][NS])
548 begin
549 if (m_arvalid[srindex[N]] && !m_arready[srindex[N]])
550 slave_raccepts[N] = 1'b0;
551 end else if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && !S_AXI_RREADY[N])
552 slave_raccepts[N] = 1'b0;
553 end
554 // }}}
555
556 // }}}
557 end for (N=NM; N<NMFULL; N=N+1)
558 begin : UNUSED_RSKID_BUFFERS
559 // {{{
560 assign w_arvalid[N] = 0;
561 assign w_araddr[N] = 0;
562 assign w_arprot[N] = 0;
563 // }}}
564 end endgenerate
565
566 // wrequested
567 // {{{
568 always @(*)
569 begin : DECONFLICT_WRITE_REQUESTS
570
571 for(iN=1; iN<NM ; iN=iN+1)
572 wrequested[iN] = 0;
573
574 // Vivado may complain about too many bits for wrequested.
575 // This is (currrently) expected. swindex is used to index
576 // into wrequested, and swindex has LGNS bits, where LGNS
577 // is $clog2(NS+1) rather than $clog2(NS). The extra bits
578 // are defined to be zeros, but the point is there are defined.
579 // Therefore, no matter what swindex is, it will always
580 // reference something valid.
581 wrequested[NM] = 0;
582
583 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
584 begin
585 wrequested[0][iM] = 1'b0;
586 for(iN=1; iN<NM ; iN=iN+1)
587 begin
588 // Continue to request any channel with
589 // a grant and pending operations
590 if (wrequest[iN-1][iM] && wgrant[iN-1][iM])
591 wrequested[iN][iM] = 1;
592 if (wrequest[iN-1][iM] && (!swgrant[iN-1]||swempty[iN-1]))
593 wrequested[iN][iM] = 1;
594 // Otherwise, if it's already claimed, then
595 // it can't be claimed again
596 if (wrequested[iN-1][iM])
597 wrequested[iN][iM] = 1;
598 end
599 wrequested[NM][iM] = wrequest[NM-1][iM] || wrequested[NM-1][iM];
600 end
601 end
602 // }}}
603
604 // rrequested
605 // {{{
606 always @(*)
607 begin : DECONFLICT_READ_REQUESTS
608
609 for(iN=0; iN<NM ; iN=iN+1)
610 rrequested[iN] = 0;
611
612 // See the note above for wrequested. This applies to
613 // rrequested as well.
614 rrequested[NM] = 0;
615
616 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
617 begin
618 rrequested[0][iM] = 0;
619 for(iN=1; iN<NM ; iN=iN+1)
620 begin
621 // Continue to request any channel with
622 // a grant and pending operations
623 if (rrequest[iN-1][iM] && rgrant[iN-1][iM])
624 rrequested[iN][iM] = 1;
625 if (rrequest[iN-1][iM] && (!srgrant[iN-1] || srempty[iN-1]))
626 rrequested[iN][iM] = 1;
627 // Otherwise, if it's already claimed, then
628 // it can't be claimed again
629 if (rrequested[iN-1][iM])
630 rrequested[iN][iM] = 1;
631 end
632 rrequested[NM][iM] = rrequest[NM-1][iM] || rrequested[NM-1][iM];
633 end
634 end
635 // }}}
636
637 // mwgrant, mrgrant
638 // {{{
639 generate for(M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
640 begin : GEN_GRANT
641 // {{{
642 always @(*)
643 begin
644 mwgrant[M] = 0;
645 for(iN=0; iN<NM; iN=iN+1)
646 if (wgrant[iN][M])
647 mwgrant[M] = 1;
648 end
649
650 always @(*)
651 begin
652 mrgrant[M] = 0;
653 for(iN=0; iN<NM; iN=iN+1)
654 if (rgrant[iN][M])
655 mrgrant[M] = 1;
656 end
657 // }}}
658 end endgenerate
659 // }}}
660
661 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
662 begin : ARBITRATE_WRITE_REQUESTS
663 // {{{
664 // Declarations
665 // {{{
666 reg stay_on_channel;
667 reg requested_channel_is_available;
668 reg leave_channel;
669 reg [LGNS-1:0] requested_index;
670 wire linger;
671 wire [NSFULL-1:0] write_requests;
672 // }}}
673
674 // stay_on_channel
675 // {{{
676 always @(*)
677 begin
678 stay_on_channel = |(wrequest[N][NS:0] & wgrant[N]);
679
680 if (swgrant[N] && !swempty[N])
681 stay_on_channel = 1;
682 end
683 // }}}
684
685 // requested_channel_is_available
686 // {{{
687 always @(*)
688 begin
689 requested_channel_is_available =
690 |(wrequest[N][NS-1:0] & ~mwgrant
691 & ~wrequested[N][NS-1:0]);
692 if (wrequest[N][NS])
693 requested_channel_is_available = 1;
694
695 if (NM < 2)
696 requested_channel_is_available = w_awvalid[N];
697 end
698 // }}}
699
700 if (OPT_LINGER == 0)
701 begin : NO_LINGER
702 // {{{
703 assign linger = 0;
704 // }}}
705 end else begin : WRITE_LINGER
706 // {{{
707 reg [LGLINGER-1:0] linger_counter;
708 reg r_linger;
709
710 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
711 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN || wgrant[N][NS])
712 begin
713 r_linger <= 0;
714 linger_counter <= 0;
715 end else if (!swempty[N] || S_AXI_BVALID[N])
716 begin
717 linger_counter <= OPT_LINGER;
718 r_linger <= 1;
719 end else if (linger_counter > 0)
720 begin
721 r_linger <= (linger_counter > 1);
722 linger_counter <= linger_counter - 1;
723 end else
724 r_linger <= 0;
725
726 assign linger = r_linger;
727
728`ifdef FORMAL
729 // {{{
730 always @(*)
731 assert(linger == (linger_counter != 0));
732 // }}}
733`endif
734 // }}}
735 end
736
737 // leave_channel
738 // {{{
739 always @(*)
740 begin
741 leave_channel = 0;
742 if (!w_awvalid[N]
743 && (!linger || wrequested[NM][swindex[N]]))
744 // Leave the channel after OPT_LINGER counts
745 // of the channel being idle, or when someone
746 // else asks for the channel
747 leave_channel = 1;
748 if (w_awvalid[N] && !wrequest[N][swindex[N]])
749 // Need to leave this channel to connect
750 // to any other channel
751 leave_channel = 1;
752 end
753 // }}}
754
755 // wgrant, swgrant
756 // {{{
757 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
758 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
759 begin
760 wgrant[N] <= 0;
761 swgrant[N] <= 0;
762 end else if (!stay_on_channel)
763 begin
764 if (requested_channel_is_available)
765 begin
766 // Switching channels
767 swgrant[N] <= 1'b1;
768 wgrant[N] <= wrequest[N][NS:0];
769 end else if (leave_channel)
770 begin
771 swgrant[N] <= 1'b0;
772 wgrant[N] <= 0;
773 end
774 end
775 // }}}
776
777 // requested_index
778 // {{{
779 assign write_requests = wrequest[N];
780
781 always @(*)
782 begin
783 requested_index = 0;
784 for(iM=0; iM<=NS; iM=iM+1)
785 if (write_requests[iM])
786 requested_index= requested_index | iM[LGNS-1:0];
787 end
788 // }}}
789
790 // Now for swindex
791 // {{{
792 reg [LGNS-1:0] r_swindex;
793
794 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
795 if (!stay_on_channel && requested_channel_is_available)
796 r_swindex <= requested_index;
797
798 assign swindex[N] = r_swindex;
799 // }}}
800 // }}}
801 end for (N=NM; N<NMFULL; N=N+1)
802 begin : EMPTY_WRITE_REQUEST
803 // {{{
804 assign swindex[N] = 0;
805 // }}}
806 end endgenerate
807
808 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
809 begin : ARBITRATE_READ_REQUESTS
810 // {{{
811 // Declarations
812 // {{{
813 reg stay_on_channel;
814 reg requested_channel_is_available;
815 reg leave_channel;
816 reg [LGNS-1:0] requested_index;
817 wire linger;
818 wire [NSFULL-1:0] read_requests;
819 // }}}
820
821 // stay_on_channel
822 // {{{
823 always @(*)
824 begin
825 stay_on_channel = |(rrequest[N][NS:0] & rgrant[N]);
826
827 if (srgrant[N] && !srempty[N])
828 stay_on_channel = 1;
829 end
830 // }}}
831
832 // requested_channel_is_available
833 // {{{
834 always @(*)
835 begin
836 requested_channel_is_available =
837 |(rrequest[N][NS-1:0] & ~mrgrant
838 & ~rrequested[N][NS-1:0]);
839 if (rrequest[N][NS])
840 requested_channel_is_available = 1;
841
842 if (NM < 2)
843 requested_channel_is_available = w_arvalid[N];
844 end
845 // }}}
846
847 if (OPT_LINGER == 0)
848 begin : NO_LINGER
849 // {{{
850 assign linger = 0;
851 // }}}
852 end else begin : READ_LINGER
853 // {{{
854 reg [LGLINGER-1:0] linger_counter;

856
857 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
858 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN || rgrant[N][NS])
859 begin
860 r_linger <= 0;
861 linger_counter <= 0;
862 end else if (!srempty[N] || S_AXI_RVALID[N])
863 begin
864 linger_counter <= OPT_LINGER;
865 r_linger <= 1;
866 end else if (linger_counter > 0)
867 begin
868 r_linger <= (linger_counter > 1);
869 linger_counter <= linger_counter - 1;
870 end else
871 r_linger <= 0;
872
873 assign linger = r_linger;
874`ifdef FORMAL

876 always @(*)
877 assert(linger == (linger_counter != 0));
878 // }}}
879`endif
880 // }}}
881 end
882
883 // leave_channel
884 // {{{
885 always @(*)
886 begin
887 leave_channel = 0;
888 if (!w_arvalid[N]
889 && (!linger || rrequested[NM][srindex[N]]))
890 // Leave the channel after OPT_LINGER counts
891 // of the channel being idle, or when someone
892 // else asks for the channel
893 leave_channel = 1;
894 if (w_arvalid[N] && !rrequest[N][srindex[N]])
895 // Need to leave this channel to connect
896 // to any other channel
897 leave_channel = 1;
898 end
899 // }}}
900
901 // rgrant, srgrant
902 // {{{
903 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
904 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
905 begin
906 rgrant[N] <= 0;
907 srgrant[N] <= 0;
908 end else if (!stay_on_channel)
909 begin
910 if (requested_channel_is_available)
911 begin
912 // Switching channels
913 srgrant[N] <= 1'b1;
914 rgrant[N] <= rrequest[N][NS:0];
915 end else if (leave_channel)
916 begin
917 srgrant[N] <= 1'b0;
918 rgrant[N] <= 0;
919 end
920 end
921 // }}}
922
923 // requested_index
924 // {{{
925 assign read_requests = rrequest[N];
926 always @(*)
927 begin
928 requested_index = 0;
929 for(iM=0; iM<=NS; iM=iM+1)
930 if (read_requests[iM])
931 requested_index = requested_index|iM[LGNS-1:0];
932 end
933 // }}}
934
935 // Now for srindex
936 // {{{
937 reg [LGNS-1:0] r_srindex;
938
939 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
940 if (!stay_on_channel && requested_channel_is_available)
941 r_srindex <= requested_index;
942
943 assign srindex[N] = r_srindex;
944 // }}}
945 // }}}
946 end for (N=NM; N<NMFULL; N=N+1)
947 begin : EMPTY_READ_REQUEST
948 // {{{
949 assign srindex[N] = 0;
950 // }}}
951 end endgenerate
952
953 // Calculate mwindex
954 generate for (M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
955 begin : SLAVE_WRITE_INDEX
956 // {{{
957 if (NM <= 1)
958 begin : ONE_MASTER
959 // {{{
960 assign mwindex[M] = 0;
961 // }}}
962 end else begin : MULTIPLE_MASTERS
963 // {{{
964 reg [LGNM-1:0] reswindex;
965 reg [LGNM-1:0] r_mwindex;
966
967 always @(*)
968 begin
969 reswindex = 0;
970 for(iN=0; iN<NM; iN=iN+1)
971 if ((!swgrant[iN] || swempty[iN])
972 &&(wrequest[iN][M] && !wrequested[iN][M]))
973 reswindex = reswindex | iN[LGNM-1:0];
974 end
975
976 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
977 if (!mwgrant[M])
978 r_mwindex <= reswindex;
979
980 assign mwindex[M] = r_mwindex;
981 // }}}
982 end
983 // }}}
984 end for (M=NS; M<NSFULL; M=M+1)
985 begin : NO_WRITE_INDEX
986 // {{{
987 assign mwindex[M] = 0;
988 // }}}
989 end endgenerate
990
991 // Calculate mrindex
992 generate for (M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
993 begin : SLAVE_READ_INDEX
994 // {{{
995 if (NM <= 1)
996 begin : ONE_MASTER
997 // {{{
998 // If there's only one master, mrindex can always
999 // point to that master--no logic required
1000 assign mrindex[M] = 0;
1001 // }}}
1002 end else begin : MULTIPLE_MASTERS
1003 // {{{
1004 reg [LGNM-1:0] resrindex;
1005 reg [LGNM-1:0] r_mrindex;
1006
1007 always @(*)
1008 begin
1009 resrindex = 0;
1010 for(iN=0; iN<NM; iN=iN+1)
1011 if ((!srgrant[iN] || srempty[iN])
1012 &&(rrequest[iN][M] && !rrequested[iN][M]))
1013 resrindex = resrindex | iN[LGNM-1:0];
1014 end
1015
1016 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1017 if (!mrgrant[M])
1018 r_mrindex <= resrindex;
1019
1020 assign mrindex[M] = r_mrindex;
1021 // }}}
1022 end
1023 // }}}
1024 end for (M=NS; M<NSFULL; M=M+1)
1025 begin : NO_READ_INDEX
1026 // {{{
1027 assign mrindex[M] = 0;
1028 // }}}
1029 end endgenerate
1030
1031 // Assign outputs to the various slaves
1032 generate for(M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
1033 begin : WRITE_SLAVE_OUTPUTS
1034 // {{{
1035
1036 // Declarations
1037 // {{{
1038 reg axi_awvalid;
1039 reg [AW-1:0] axi_awaddr;
1040 reg [2:0] axi_awprot;
1041
1042 reg axi_wvalid;
1043 reg [DW-1:0] axi_wdata;
1044 reg [DW/8-1:0] axi_wstrb;
1045 //
1046 reg axi_bready;
1047
1048 wire sawstall, swstall, mbstall;
1049 // }}}
1050 assign sawstall= (M_AXI_AWVALID[M]&& !M_AXI_AWREADY[M]);
1051 assign swstall = (M_AXI_WVALID[M] && !M_AXI_WREADY[M]);
1052 assign mbstall = (S_AXI_BVALID[mwindex[M]] && !S_AXI_BREADY[mwindex[M]]);
1053
1054 // axi_awvalid
1055 // {{{
1056 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1057 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN || !mwgrant[M])
1058 axi_awvalid <= 0;
1059 else if (!sawstall)
1060 begin
1061 axi_awvalid <= w_awvalid[mwindex[M]]
1062 &&(slave_awaccepts[mwindex[M]]);
1063 end
1064 // }}}
1065
1066 // axi_awaddr, axi_awprot
1067 // {{{
1068 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1069 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !S_AXI_ARESETN)
1070 begin
1071 axi_awaddr <= 0;
1072 axi_awprot <= 0;
1073 end else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !mwgrant[M])
1074 begin
1075 axi_awaddr <= 0;
1076 axi_awprot <= 0;
1077 end else if (!sawstall)
1078 begin
1079 if (!OPT_LOWPOWER||(w_awvalid[mwindex[M]]&&slave_awaccepts[mwindex[M]]))
1080 begin
1081 axi_awaddr <= m_awaddr[mwindex[M]];
1082 axi_awprot <= m_awprot[mwindex[M]];
1083 end else begin
1084 axi_awaddr <= 0;
1085 axi_awprot <= 0;
1086 end
1087 end
1088 // }}}
1089
1090 // axi_wvalid
1091 // {{{
1092 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1093 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN || !mwgrant[M])
1094 axi_wvalid <= 0;
1095 else if (!swstall)
1096 begin
1097 axi_wvalid <= (w_wvalid[mwindex[M]])
1098 &&(slave_waccepts[mwindex[M]]);
1099 end
1100 // }}}
1101
1102 // axi_wdata, axi_wstrb
1103 // {{{
1104 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1105 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !S_AXI_ARESETN)
1106 begin
1107 axi_wdata <= 0;
1108 axi_wstrb <= 0;
1109 end else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !mwgrant[M])
1110 begin
1111 axi_wdata <= 0;
1112 axi_wstrb <= 0;
1113 end else if (!swstall)
1114 begin
1115 if (!OPT_LOWPOWER || (w_wvalid[mwindex[M]]&&slave_waccepts[mwindex[M]]))
1116 begin
1117 axi_wdata <= m_wdata[mwindex[M]];
1118 axi_wstrb <= m_wstrb[mwindex[M]];
1119 end else begin
1120 axi_wdata <= 0;
1121 axi_wstrb <= 0;
1122 end
1123 end
1124 // }}}
1125
1126 // axi_bready
1127 // {{{
1128 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1129 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN || !mwgrant[M])
1130 axi_bready <= 1;
1131 else if (!mbstall)
1132 axi_bready <= 1;
1133 else if (M_AXI_BVALID[M]) // && mbstall
1134 axi_bready <= 0;
1135 // }}}
1136
1137 //
1138 assign M_AXI_AWVALID[M] = axi_awvalid;
1139 assign M_AXI_AWADDR[M*AW +: AW] = axi_awaddr;
1140 assign M_AXI_AWPROT[M*3 +: 3] = axi_awprot;
1141 //
1142 //
1143 assign M_AXI_WVALID[M] = axi_wvalid;
1144 assign M_AXI_WDATA[M*DW +: DW] = axi_wdata;
1145 assign M_AXI_WSTRB[M*DW/8 +: DW/8] = axi_wstrb;
1146 //
1147 //
1148 assign M_AXI_BREADY[M] = axi_bready;
1149 //
1150`ifdef FORMAL
1151 // {{{
1152 if (OPT_LOWPOWER)
1153 begin
1154 always @(*)
1155 if (!axi_awvalid)
1156 begin
1157 assert(axi_awaddr == 0);
1158 assert(axi_awprot == 0);
1159 end
1160
1161 always @(*)
1162 if (!axi_wvalid)
1163 begin
1164 assert(axi_wdata == 0);
1165 assert(axi_wstrb == 0);
1166 end
1167 end
1168 // }}}
1169`endif
1170 // }}}
1171 end endgenerate
1172
1173
1174 generate for(M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
1175 begin : READ_SLAVE_OUTPUTS
1176 // {{{
1177 // Declarations
1178 // {{{
1179 reg axi_arvalid;
1180 reg [C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] axi_araddr;
1181 reg [2:0] axi_arprot;
1182 //
1183 reg axi_rready;
1184
1185 wire arstall, srstall;
1186 // }}}
1187 assign arstall= (M_AXI_ARVALID[M]&& !M_AXI_ARREADY[M]);
1188 assign srstall = (S_AXI_RVALID[mrindex[M]]
1189 && !S_AXI_RREADY[mrindex[M]]);
1190
1191 // axi_arvalid
1192 // {{{
1193 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)

1195 axi_arvalid <= 0;
1196 else if (!arstall)
1197 begin
1198 axi_arvalid <= w_arvalid[mrindex[M]] && slave_raccepts[mrindex[M]];
1199 end
1200 // }}}
1201
1202 // axi_araddr, axi_arprot
1203 // {{{
1204 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1205 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !S_AXI_ARESETN)
1206 begin
1207 axi_araddr <= 0;
1208 axi_arprot <= 0;
1209 end else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !mrgrant[M])
1210 begin
1211 axi_araddr <= 0;
1212 axi_arprot <= 0;
1213 end else if (!arstall)
1214 begin
1215 if (!OPT_LOWPOWER || (w_arvalid[mrindex[M]] && slave_raccepts[mrindex[M]]))
1216 begin
1217 if (NM == 1)
1218 begin
1219 axi_araddr <= w_araddr[0];
1220 axi_arprot <= w_arprot[0];
1221 end else begin
1222 axi_araddr <= w_araddr[mrindex[M]];
1223 axi_arprot <= w_arprot[mrindex[M]];
1224 end
1225 end else begin
1226 axi_araddr <= 0;
1227 axi_arprot <= 0;
1228 end
1229 end
1230 // }}}
1231
1232 // axi_rready
1233 // {{{
1234 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1235 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN || !mrgrant[M])
1236 axi_rready <= 1;
1237 else if (!srstall)
1238 axi_rready <= 1;
1239 else if (M_AXI_RVALID[M] && M_AXI_RREADY[M]) // && srstall
1240 axi_rready <= 0;
1241 // }}}
1242
1243 //
1244 assign M_AXI_ARVALID[M] = axi_arvalid;
1245 assign M_AXI_ARADDR[M*AW +: AW] = axi_araddr;
1246 assign M_AXI_ARPROT[M*3 +: 3] = axi_arprot;
1247 //
1248 assign M_AXI_RREADY[M] = axi_rready;
1249 //
1250`ifdef FORMAL
1251 // {{{
1252 if (OPT_LOWPOWER)
1253 begin
1254 always @(*)
1255 if (!axi_arvalid)
1256 begin

1269 // {{{
1270 reg axi_bvalid;

1273 wire [1:0] i_axi_bresp;
1274 wire mbstall;

1276 always @(*)
1277 if (wgrant[N][NS])

1279 else
1280 i_axi_bvalid = m_bvalid[swindex[N]];

1292 r_bvalid[N] <= swgrant[N] && i_axi_bvalid;

1294 r_bvalid[N] <= 1'b0;
1295 // }}}
1296
1297 // r_bresp
1298 // {{{
1299 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1300 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !S_AXI_ARESETN)
1301 r_bresp[N] <= 0;
1302 else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && (!swgrant[N] || S_AXI_BREADY[N]))
1303 r_bresp[N] <= 0;
1304 else if (!r_bvalid[N])
1305 begin
1306 if (!OPT_LOWPOWER ||(i_axi_bvalid && !wgrant[N][NS] && mbstall))
1307 begin
1308 r_bresp[N] <= i_axi_bresp;
1309 end else
1310 r_bresp[N] <= 0;
1311 end
1312 // }}}
1313
1314 // axi_bvalid
1315 // {{{
1316 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1317 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1318 axi_bvalid <= 0;
1319 else if (!mbstall)
1320 axi_bvalid <= swgrant[N] && (r_bvalid[N] || i_axi_bvalid);
1321 // }}}
1322
1323 // axi_bresp
1324 // {{{
1325 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1326 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !S_AXI_ARESETN)
1327 axi_bresp <= 0;
1328 else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !swgrant[N])
1329 axi_bresp <= 0;
1330 else if (!mbstall)
1331 begin
1332 if (r_bvalid[N])
1333 axi_bresp <= r_bresp[N];
1334 else if (!OPT_LOWPOWER || i_axi_bvalid)
1335 axi_bresp <= i_axi_bresp;
1336 else
1337 axi_bresp <= 0;
1338
1339 if (wgrant[N][NS] && (!OPT_LOWPOWER || i_axi_bvalid))
1340 axi_bresp <= INTERCONNECT_ERROR;
1341 end
1342 // }}}
1343

1349 always @(*)

1351 assert(r_bresp[N] != 2'b01);
1352 always @(*)
1353 if (swgrant[N])
1354 assert(m_bready[swindex[N]] == !r_bvalid[N]);
1355 else
1356 assert(!r_bvalid[N]);
1357 always @(*)
1358 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !r_bvalid[N])
1359 assert(r_bresp[N] == 0);
1360
1361 always @(*)
1362 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !axi_bvalid)
1363 assert(axi_bresp == 0);
1364 // }}}
1365`endif
1366 // }}}
1367 end endgenerate

1400

1434 r_rdata[N] <= 0;

1437

1509 // Count pending transactions
1510 generate for (N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
1511 begin : COUNT_PENDING
1512 // {{{
1513 reg [LGMAXBURST-1:0] awpending, rpending,
1514 missing_wdata;
1515 //reg rempty, awempty; // wempty;
1516 reg r_wdata_expected;
1517
1518 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1519 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1520 begin
1521 awpending <= 0;
1522 swempty[N] <= 1;
1523 swfull[N] <= 0;
1524 end else case ({(w_awvalid[N] && slave_awaccepts[N]),
1525 (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && S_AXI_BREADY[N])})
1526 2'b01: begin
1527 awpending <= awpending - 1;
1528 swempty[N] <= (awpending <= 1);
1529 swfull[N] <= 0;
1530 end
1531 2'b10: begin
1532 awpending <= awpending + 1;
1533 swempty[N] <= 0;
1534 swfull[N] <= &awpending[LGMAXBURST-1:1];
1535 end
1536 default: begin end
1537 endcase
1538
1539 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1540 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1541 missing_wdata <= 0;
1542 else begin
1543 missing_wdata <= missing_wdata
1544 +((w_awvalid[N] && slave_awaccepts[N])? 1:0)
1545 -((w_wvalid[N] && slave_waccepts[N])? 1:0);
1546 end
1547
1548 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1549 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1550 r_wdata_expected <= 0;
1551 else case({ w_awvalid[N] && slave_awaccepts[N],
1552 w_wvalid[N] && slave_waccepts[N] })
1553 2'b10: r_wdata_expected <= 1;
1554 2'b01: r_wdata_expected <= (missing_wdata > 1);
1555 default: begin end
1556 endcase
1557
1558
1559 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1560 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1561 begin
1562 rpending <= 0;
1563 srempty[N]<= 1;
1564 srfull[N] <= 0;
1565 end else case ({(w_arvalid[N] && slave_raccepts[N]),
1566 (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && S_AXI_RREADY[N])})
1567 2'b01: begin
1568 rpending <= rpending - 1;
1569 srempty[N] <= (rpending == 1);
1570 srfull[N] <= 0;
1571 end
1572 2'b10: begin
1573 rpending <= rpending + 1;
1574 srfull[N] <= &rpending[LGMAXBURST-1:1];
1575 srempty[N] <= 0;
1576 end
1577 default: begin end
1578 endcase
1579
1580 assign w_sawpending[N] = awpending;
1581 assign w_srpending[N] = rpending;
1582
1583 assign wdata_expected[N] = r_wdata_expected;
1584
1585`ifdef FORMAL
1586 // {{{
1587 reg [LGMAXBURST-1:0] wpending;
1588 reg [LGMAXBURST-1:0] f_missing_wdata;
1589
1590 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1591 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1592 wpending <= 0;
1593 else case ({(w_wvalid[N] && slave_waccepts[N]),
1594 (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && S_AXI_BREADY[N])})
1595 2'b01: wpending <= wpending - 1;
1596 2'b10: wpending <= wpending + 1;
1597 default: begin end
1598 endcase
1599
1600 assign w_swpending[N] = wpending;
1601
1602 always @(*)
1603 assert(missing_wdata == awpending - wpending);
1604 always @(*)
1605 assert(r_wdata_expected == (missing_wdata > 0));
1606 always @(*)
1607 assert(awpending >= wpending);
1608 // }}}
1609`endif
1610 // }}}
1611 end endgenerate

18872 +((OPT_BUFFER_DECODER & dcd_arvalid[N]) ? 1:0)
18882 +(S_AXI_RVALID[N] ? 1:0));
18892
18902 always @(*)
18912 if (S_AXI_ARESETN && !srgrant[N])
18922 begin
18932 assert(!S_AXI_RVALID[N]);
18942 assert(fm_rd_outstanding[N]== (S_AXI_ARREADY[N] ? 0:1)
18952 +((OPT_BUFFER_DECODER && dcd_arvalid[N])? 1:0));
18962 assert(w_srpending[N] == 0);
18972 end
18982
18992 //
19002 // Check full/empty flags
19012 //
19022 localparam [LGMAXBURST-1:0] NEAR_THRESHOLD = -2;
19032
19042 always @(*)
19052 begin
19062 assert(swfull[N] == &w_sawpending[N]);
19072 assert(swempty[N] == (w_sawpending[N] == 0));
19082 end
19092
19102 always @(*)
19112 begin
19122 assert(srfull[N] == &w_srpending[N]);
19132 assert(srempty[N] == (w_srpending[N] == 0));
19142 end
19152 // }}}
19162 end endgenerate
19172
1918 generate for(M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
1919 begin : CHECK_SLAVES
1920 // {{{
1921 faxil_master #(
1922 .C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH(DW),
1923 .C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH(AW),
1924 .F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET(1'b1),
1925 .F_AXI_MAXRSTALL(0),

1947 .i_axi_arprot( M_AXI_ARPROT[M*3 +: 3]),

1950 .i_axi_rvalid(M_AXI_RVALID[M]),
1951 .i_axi_rready(M_AXI_RREADY[M]),

1954 //

1958

1996 begin : CORRELATE_OUTSTANDING

2000 begin

2002 - (S_AXI_AWREADY[N] ? 0:1)

2010 - (S_AXI_WREADY[N] ? 0:1)

2048 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2049 //
2050 // Cover properties
2051 // {{{
2052 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2053 //
2054 //
2055 // Can every master reach every slave?
2056 // Can things transition without dropping the request line(s)?
2057 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
2058 begin : COVER_CONNECTIVITY_FROM_MASTER
2059 reg [3:0] cvr_w_returns, cvr_r_returns;
2060 reg err_wr_return, err_rd_return;
2061 reg [NS-1:0] cvr_w_every, cvr_r_every;
2062 reg cvr_was_wevery, cvr_was_revery,
2063 cvr_whsreturn, cvr_rhsreturn;
2064
2065 // cvr_w_returns is a speed check: Can we return one write
2066 // acknowledgement per clock cycle?
2067 initial cvr_w_returns = 0;
2068 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2069 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2070 cvr_w_returns = 0;
2071 else begin
2072 cvr_w_returns <= { cvr_w_returns[2:0], 1'b0 };
2073 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && S_AXI_BREADY[N] && !wgrant[N][NS])
2074 cvr_w_returns[0] <= 1'b1;
2075 end
2076
2077 initial cvr_whsreturn = 0;
2078 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2079 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2080 cvr_whsreturn <= 0;
2081 else
2082 cvr_whsreturn <= cvr_whsreturn || (&cvr_w_returns);
2083
2084 // w_every is a connectivity test: Can we get a return from
2085 // every slave?
2086 initial cvr_w_every = 0;
2087 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2088 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2089 cvr_w_every <= 0;
2090 else if (!S_AXI_AWVALID[N])
2091 cvr_w_every <= 0;
2092 else begin
2093 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && S_AXI_BREADY[N] && !wgrant[N][NS])
2094 cvr_w_every[swindex[N]] <= 1'b1;
2095 end
2096
2097 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2098 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N])
2099 assert($stable(swindex[N]));
2100
2101 initial cvr_was_wevery = 0;
2102 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2103 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2104 cvr_was_wevery <= 0;
2105 else
2106 cvr_was_wevery <= cvr_was_wevery || (&cvr_w_every);
2107
2108 // err_wr_return is a test to make certain we can return a
2109 // bus error on the write channel.
2110 initial err_wr_return = 0;
2111 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2112 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2113 err_wr_return = 0;
2114 else if (wgrant[N][NS] && S_AXI_BVALID[N]
2115 && (S_AXI_BRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR))
2116 err_wr_return = 1;
2117
2118`ifndef VERILATOR
2119 always @(*)
2120 cover(!swgrant[N] && cvr_whsreturn);
2121 always @(*)
2122 cover(!swgrant[N] && cvr_was_wevery);
2123
2124 always @(*)
2125 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && wrequest[N][NS]);
2126 always @(*)
2127 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && wrequest[N][NS] && slave_awaccepts[N]);
2128 always @(*)
2129 cover(err_wr_return);
2130 always @(*)
2131 cover(!swgrant[N] && err_wr_return);
2132`endif
2133
2134 always @(*)
2135 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N])
2136 assert(swgrant[N]);
2137
2138 // cvr_r_returns is a speed check: Can we return one read
2139 // acknowledgment per clock cycle?
2140 initial cvr_r_returns = 0;
2141 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2142 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2143 cvr_r_returns = 0;
2144 else begin
2145 cvr_r_returns <= { cvr_r_returns[2:0], 1'b0 };
2146 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && S_AXI_RREADY[N])
2147 cvr_r_returns[0] <= 1'b1;
2148 end
2149
2150 initial cvr_rhsreturn = 0;
2151 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2152 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2153 cvr_rhsreturn <= 0;
2154 else
2155 cvr_rhsreturn <= cvr_rhsreturn || (&cvr_r_returns);
2156
2157
2158 // r_every is a connectivity test: Can we get a read return from
2159 // every slave?
2160 initial cvr_r_every = 0;
2161 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2162 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2163 cvr_r_every = 0;
2164 else if (!S_AXI_ARVALID[N])
2165 cvr_r_every = 0;
2166 else begin
2167 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && S_AXI_RREADY[N])
2168 cvr_r_every[srindex[N]] <= 1'b1;
2169 end
2170
2171 // cvr_was_revery is a return to idle check following the
2172 // connectivity test. Since the connectivity test is cleared
2173 // if there's ever a drop in the valid line, we need a separate
2174 // wire to check that this master can return to idle again.
2175 initial cvr_was_revery = 0;
2176 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2177 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2178 cvr_was_revery <= 0;
2179 else
2180 cvr_was_revery <= cvr_was_revery || (&cvr_r_every);
2181
2182 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2183 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N])
2184 assert($stable(srindex[N]));
2185
2186 initial err_rd_return = 0;
2187 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2188 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2189 err_rd_return = 0;
2190 else if (rgrant[N][NS] && S_AXI_RVALID[N]
2191 && (S_AXI_RRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR))
2192 err_rd_return = 1;
2193
2194`ifndef VERILATOR
2195 always @(*)
2196 cover(!srgrant[N] && cvr_rhsreturn); // @26
2197 always @(*)
2198 cover(!srgrant[N] && cvr_was_revery); // @26
2199
2200 always @(*)
2201 cover(S_AXI_ARVALID[N] && rrequest[N][NS]);
2202 always @(*)
2203 cover(rgrant[N][NS]);
2204 always @(*)
2205 cover(err_rd_return);
2206 always @(*)
2207 cover(!srgrant[N] && err_rd_return); //@!
2208`endif
2209
2210 always @(*)
2211 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && wgrant[N][NS])
2212 assert(S_AXI_BRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR);
2213 always @(*)
2214 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && rgrant[N][NS])
2215 assert(S_AXI_RRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR);
2216 end endgenerate
2217
2218 reg cvr_multi_write_hit, cvr_multi_read_hit;
2219
2220 initial cvr_multi_write_hit = 0;
2221 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2222 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2223 cvr_multi_write_hit <= 0;
2224 else if (fm_awr_outstanding[0] > 2 && !wgrant[0][NS])
2225 cvr_multi_write_hit <= 1;
2226
2227 initial cvr_multi_read_hit = 0;
2228 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2229 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2230 cvr_multi_read_hit <= 0;
2231 else if (fm_rd_outstanding[0] > 2 && !rgrant[0][NS])
2232 cvr_multi_read_hit <= 1;
2233
2234 always @(*)
2235 cover(cvr_multi_write_hit);
2236
2237 always @(*)
2238 cover(cvr_multi_read_hit);
2239
2240 always @(*)
2241 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && cvr_multi_write_hit & mwgrant == 0 && M_AXI_BVALID == 0);
2242
2243 always @(*)
2244 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && cvr_multi_read_hit & mrgrant == 0 && M_AXI_RVALID == 0);
2245 // }}}
2246 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2247 //
2248 // Negation check
2249 // {{{
2250 // Pick a particular value. Assume the value doesn't show up on the
2251 // input. Prove it doesn't show up on the output. This will check for
2252 // ...
2253 // 1. Stuck bits on the output channel
2254 // 2. Cross-talk between channels
2255 //
2256 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2257 //
2258 //
2259 (* anyconst *) reg [LGNM-1:0] f_const_source;
2260 (* anyconst *) reg [AW-1:0] f_const_addr;
2261 (* anyconst *) reg [AW-1:0] f_const_addr_n;
2262 (* anyconst *) reg [DW-1:0] f_const_data_n;
2263 (* anyconst *) reg [DW/8-1:0] f_const_strb_n;
2264 (* anyconst *) reg [3-1:0] f_const_prot_n;
2265 (* anyconst *) reg [2-1:0] f_const_resp_n;
2266 reg [LGNS-1:0] f_const_slave;
2267
2268 always @(*)
2269 assume(f_const_source < NM);
2270 always @(*)
2271 begin
2272 f_const_slave = NS;
2273 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
2274 begin
2275 if (((f_const_addr ^ SLAVE_ADDR[iM*AW+:AW])
2276 &SLAVE_MASK[iM*AW+:AW])==0)
2277 f_const_slave = iM;
2278 end
2279
2280 assume(f_const_slave < NS);
2281 end
2282
2283 reg [AW-1:0] f_awaddr;
2284 reg [AW-1:0] f_araddr;
2285 always @(*)
2286 f_awaddr = S_AXI_AWADDR[f_const_source * AW +: AW];
2287 always @(*)
2288 f_araddr = S_AXI_ARADDR[f_const_source * AW +: AW];
2289
2290 // The assumption check: assume our negated values are not found on
2291 // the inputs
2292 always @(*)
2293 begin
2294 if (S_AXI_AWVALID[f_const_source])
2295 begin
2296 assume(f_awaddr != f_const_addr_n);
2297 assume(S_AXI_AWPROT[f_const_source*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2298 end
2299 if (w_wvalid)
2300 begin
2301 assume(m_wdata[f_const_source] != f_const_data_n);
2302 assume(m_wstrb[f_const_source] != f_const_strb_n);
2303 end
2304 if (S_AXI_ARVALID[f_const_source])
2305 begin
2306 assume(f_araddr != f_const_addr_n);
2307 assume(S_AXI_ARPROT[f_const_source*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2308 end
2309
2310 if (M_AXI_BVALID[f_const_slave] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2311 begin
2312 assume(m_bresp[f_const_slave] != f_const_resp_n);
2313 end
2314
2315 if (M_AXI_RVALID[f_const_slave] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2316 begin
2317 assume(m_rdata[f_const_slave] != f_const_data_n);
2318 assume(m_rresp[f_const_slave] != f_const_resp_n);
2319 end
2320 end
2321
2322 // Proof check: Prove these values are not found on our outputs
2323 always @(*)
2324 begin
2325 if (skd_awvalid[f_const_source])
2326 begin
2327 assert(skd_awaddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2328 assert(skd_awprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2329 end
2330 if (dcd_awvalid[f_const_source])
2331 begin
2332 assert(m_awaddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2333 assert(m_awprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2334 end
2335 if (M_AXI_AWVALID[f_const_slave] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2336 begin
2337 assert(M_AXI_AWADDR[f_const_slave*AW+:AW] != f_const_addr_n);
2338 assert(M_AXI_AWPROT[f_const_slave*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2339 end
2340 if (M_AXI_WVALID[f_const_slave] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2341 begin
2342 assert(M_AXI_WDATA[f_const_slave*DW+:DW] != f_const_data_n);
2343 assert(M_AXI_WSTRB[f_const_slave*(DW/8)+:(DW/8)] != f_const_strb_n);
2344 end
2345 if (skd_arvalid[f_const_source])
2346 begin
2347 assert(skd_araddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2348 assert(skd_arprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2349 end
2350 if (dcd_arvalid[f_const_source])
2351 begin
2352 assert(w_araddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2353 assert(w_arprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2354 end
2355 if (M_AXI_ARVALID[f_const_slave] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2356 begin
2357 assert(M_AXI_ARADDR[f_const_slave*AW+:AW] != f_const_addr_n);
2358 assert(M_AXI_ARPROT[f_const_slave*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2359 end
2360 //
2361 if (r_bvalid[f_const_source] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2362 assert(r_bresp[f_const_source] != f_const_resp_n);
2363 if (S_AXI_BVALID[f_const_source] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2364 assert(S_AXI_BRESP[f_const_source*2+:2] != f_const_resp_n);
2365 if (r_rvalid[f_const_source] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2366 begin
2367 assert(r_rresp[f_const_source] != f_const_resp_n);
2368 assert(r_rdata[f_const_source] != f_const_data_n);
2369 end
2370 if (S_AXI_RVALID[f_const_source] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2371 begin
2372 assert(S_AXI_RRESP[f_const_source*2+:2]!=f_const_resp_n);
2373 assert(S_AXI_RDATA[f_const_source*DW+:DW]!=f_const_data_n);
2374 end
2375 end
2376 // }}}
2377 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2378 //
2379 // (Careless) constraining assumptions
2380 // {{{
2381 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2382 //
2383 //
2384 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
2385 begin
2386
2387 end endgenerate
2388 // }}}
2389`endif
2390// }}}
2391endmodule

2393`default_nettype wire
2394`endif

candidate/axilxbar.v

1////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2//
3// Filename: rtl/axilxbar.v
4// {{{
5// Project: WB2AXIPSP: bus bridges and other odds and ends
6//
7// Purpose: Create a full crossbar between NM AXI-lite sources (masters),
8// and NS AXI-lite slaves. Every master can talk to any slave,
9// provided it isn't already busy.
10//
11// Performance: This core has been designed with the goal of being able to push
12// one transaction through the interconnect, from any master to
13// any slave, per clock cycle. This may perhaps be its most unique
14// feature. While throughput is good, latency is something else.
15//
16// The arbiter requires a clock to switch, then another clock to send data
17// downstream. This creates a minimum two clock latency up front. The
18// return path suffers another clock of latency as well, placing the
19// minimum latency at four clocks. The minimum write latency is at
20// least one clock longer, since the write data must wait for the write
21// address before proceeeding.
22//
23// Usage: To use, you must first set NM and NS to the number of masters
24// and the number of slaves you wish to connect to. You then need to
25// adjust the addresses of the slaves, found SLAVE_ADDR array. Those
26// bits that are relevant in SLAVE_ADDR to then also be set in SLAVE_MASK.
27// Adjusting the data and address widths go without saying.
28//
29// Lower numbered masters are given priority in any "fight".
30//
31// Channel grants are given on the condition that 1) they are requested,
32// 2) no other channel has a grant, 3) all of the responses have been
33// received from the current channel, and 4) the internal counters are
34// not overflowing.
35//
36// The core limits the number of outstanding transactions on any channel to
37// 1<<LGMAXBURST-1.
38//
39// Channel grants are lost 1) after OPT_LINGER clocks of being idle, or
40// 2) when another master requests an idle (but still lingering) channel
41// assignment, or 3) once all the responses have been returned to the
42// current channel, and the current master is requesting another channel.
43//
44// A special slave is allocated for the case of no valid address.
45//
46// Since the write channel has no address information, the write data
47// channel always be delayed by at least one clock from the write address
48// channel.
49//
50// If OPT_LOWPOWER is set, then unused values will be set to zero.
51// This can also be used to help identify relevant values within any
52// trace.
53//
54//
55// Creator: Dan Gisselquist, Ph.D.
