1707 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
1708 begin : CHECK_MASTER_GRANTS
1709 // {{{
1710
1711 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
1712 // Write grant checks
1713 // {{{
1714 always @(*)
1715 for(iM=0; iM<=NS; iM=iM+1)
1716 begin
1717 if (wgrant[N][iM])
1718 begin
1719 assert((wgrant[N] ^ (1<<iM))==0);
1720 assert(swgrant[N]);
1721 assert(swindex[N] == iM);
1722 if (iM < NS)
1723 begin
1724 assert(mwgrant[iM]);
1725 assert(mwindex[iM] == N);
1726 end
1727 end
1728 end
1729
1730 always @(*)
1731 if (swgrant[N])
1732 assert(wgrant[N] != 0);
1733
1734 always @(*)
1735 if (wrequest[N][NS])
1736 assert(wrequest[N][NS-1:0] == 0);
1737
1738 // }}}
1739 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
1740 //
1741 // Read grant checking
1742 // {{{
17431 always @(*)
17441 begin
17451 // Grant and valid must agree for the read channel.
17461 assert(srgrant[N] == (rgrant[N] != 0));
17471
17481 if (srgrant[N])
17491 begin
17501 // Index must be a valid route index: 0..NS inclusive.
17511 assert(srindex[N] <= NS);
17521
17531 // Exactly one selected route, and it matches srindex.
17541 assert(rgrant[N] == ({{(NS){1'b0}}, 1'b1} << srindex[N]));
17551
17561 // If a real slave is selected, reciprocal slave-side
17571 // grant/index must agree.
17581 if (srindex[N] < NS)
17591 begin
17601 assert(mrgrant[srindex[N]]);
17611 assert(mrindex[srindex[N]] == N);
17621 end
17631 end
17641
17651 // Error route is exclusive of real slave routes.
17661 if (rrequest[N][NS])
17671 assert(rrequest[N][NS-1:0] == 0);
17681 end
1769 // }}}
1770 // }}}
1771 end endgenerate
1772
1773 generate for(M=0; M<NS; M=M+1)
1774 begin : CHECK_SLAVES
1775 // {{{
1776 faxil_master #(
1777 .C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH(DW),
1778 .C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH(AW),
1779 .F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET(1'b1),
1780 .F_AXI_MAXRSTALL(0),
1781 .F_LGDEPTH(F_LGDEPTH))
1782 slvi(.i_clk(S_AXI_ACLK),
1783 .i_axi_reset_n(S_AXI_ARESETN),
1784 //
1785 .i_axi_awvalid(M_AXI_AWVALID[M]),
1786 .i_axi_awready(M_AXI_AWREADY[M]),
1787 .i_axi_awaddr(M_AXI_AWADDR[M*AW +: AW]),
1788 .i_axi_awprot(M_AXI_AWPROT[M*3 +: 3]),
1789 //
1790 .i_axi_wvalid(M_AXI_WVALID[M]),
1791 .i_axi_wready(M_AXI_WREADY[M]),
1792 .i_axi_wdata( M_AXI_WDATA[M*DW +: DW]),
1793 .i_axi_wstrb( M_AXI_WSTRB[M*DW/8 +: DW/8]),
1794 //
1795 .i_axi_bvalid(M_AXI_BVALID[M]),
1796 .i_axi_bready(M_AXI_BREADY[M]),
1797 .i_axi_bresp( M_AXI_BRESP[M*2 +: 2]),
1798 //
1799 .i_axi_arvalid(M_AXI_ARVALID[M]),
1800 .i_axi_arready(M_AXI_ARREADY[M]),
1801 .i_axi_araddr( M_AXI_ARADDR[M*AW +: AW]),
1802 .i_axi_arprot( M_AXI_ARPROT[M*3 +: 3]),
1803 //
1804 //
1805 .i_axi_rvalid(M_AXI_RVALID[M]),
1806 .i_axi_rready(M_AXI_RREADY[M]),
1807 .i_axi_rdata( M_AXI_RDATA[M*DW +: DW]),
1808 .i_axi_rresp( M_AXI_RRESP[M*2 +: 2]),
1809 //
1810 .f_axi_rd_outstanding( fs_rd_outstanding[M]),
1811 .f_axi_wr_outstanding( fs_wr_outstanding[M]),
1812 .f_axi_awr_outstanding(fs_awr_outstanding[M]));
1813
1814 always @(*)
1815 assert(fs_wr_outstanding[M] + (M_AXI_WVALID[M] ? 1:0)
1816 <= fs_awr_outstanding[M] + (M_AXI_AWVALID[M]? 1:0));
1817
1818 always @(*)
1819 if (!mwgrant[M])
1820 begin
1821 assert(fs_awr_outstanding[M] == 0);
1822 assert(fs_wr_outstanding[M] == 0);
1823 end
1824
1825 always @(*)
1826 if (!mrgrant[M])
1827 assert(fs_rd_outstanding[M] == 0);
1828
1829 always @(*)
1830 assert(fs_awr_outstanding[M] < { 1'b1, {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b0}} });
1831 always @(*)
1832 assert(fs_wr_outstanding[M] < { 1'b1, {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b0}} });
1833 always @(*)
1834 assert(fs_rd_outstanding[M] < { 1'b1, {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b0}} });
1835
1836 always @(*)
1837 if (M_AXI_AWVALID[M])
1838 assert(((M_AXI_AWADDR[M*AW +: AW]
1839 ^ SLAVE_ADDR[M*AW +: AW])
1840 & SLAVE_MASK[M*AW +: AW]) == 0);
1841
1842 always @(*)
1843 if (M_AXI_ARVALID[M])
1844 assert(((M_AXI_ARADDR[M*AW +: AW]
1845 ^ SLAVE_ADDR[M*AW +: AW])
1846 & SLAVE_MASK[M*AW +: AW]) == 0);
1847 // }}}
1848 end endgenerate
1849
1850 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
1851 begin : CORRELATE_OUTSTANDING
1852 // {{{
1853 always @(*)
1854 if (S_AXI_ARESETN && (swgrant[N] && (swindex[N] < NS)))
1855 begin
1856 assert((fm_awr_outstanding[N]
1857 - (S_AXI_AWREADY[N] ? 0:1)
1858 -((OPT_BUFFER_DECODER && dcd_awvalid[N]) ? 1:0)
1859 - (S_AXI_BVALID[N] ? 1:0))
1860 == (fs_awr_outstanding[swindex[N]]
1861 + (m_awvalid[swindex[N]] ? 1:0)
1862 + (m_bready[swindex[N]] ? 0:1)));
1863
1864 assert((fm_wr_outstanding[N]
1865 - (S_AXI_WREADY[N] ? 0:1)
1866 - (S_AXI_BVALID[N] ? 1:0))
1867 == (fs_wr_outstanding[swindex[N]]
1868 + (m_wvalid[swindex[N]] ? 1:0)
1869 + (m_bready[swindex[N]] ? 0:1)));
1870
1871 end else if (S_AXI_ARESETN && (!swgrant[N] || (swindex[N]==NS)))
1872 begin
1873 if (!swgrant[N])
1874 assert(fm_awr_outstanding[N] ==
1875 (S_AXI_AWREADY[N] ? 0:1)
1876 +((OPT_BUFFER_DECODER && dcd_awvalid[N]) ? 1:0)
1877 +(S_AXI_BVALID[N] ? 1:0));
1878 else
1879 assert(fm_awr_outstanding[N] >=
1880 (S_AXI_AWREADY[N] ? 0:1)
1881 +((OPT_BUFFER_DECODER && dcd_awvalid[N]) ? 1:0)
1882 +(S_AXI_BVALID[N] ? 1:0));
1883
1884 assert(fm_wr_outstanding[N] ==
1885 (S_AXI_WREADY[N] ? 0:1)
1886 +(S_AXI_BVALID[N] ? 1:0));
1887 end
1888
1889 always @(*)
1890 if (srgrant[N] && (srindex[N] < NS))
1891 begin
1892 assert((fm_rd_outstanding[N]//17
1893 - (S_AXI_ARREADY[N] ? 0:1)//1
1894 -((OPT_BUFFER_DECODER && dcd_arvalid[N]) ? 1:0)
1895 - (S_AXI_RVALID[N] ? 1:0))//0
1896 == (fs_rd_outstanding[srindex[N]]//16
1897 + (m_arvalid[srindex[N]] ? 1:0)//0
1898 + (m_rready[srindex[N]] ? 0:1)));//0
1899 end
1900 // }}}
1901 end endgenerate
1902
1903 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
1904 //
1905 // Cover properties
1906 // {{{
1907 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
1908 //
1909 //
1910 // Can every master reach every slave?
1911 // Can things transition without dropping the request line(s)?
1912 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
1913 begin : COVER_CONNECTIVITY_FROM_MASTER
1914 reg [3:0] cvr_w_returns, cvr_r_returns;
1915 reg err_wr_return, err_rd_return;
1916 reg [NS-1:0] cvr_w_every, cvr_r_every;
1917 reg cvr_was_wevery, cvr_was_revery,
1918 cvr_whsreturn, cvr_rhsreturn;
1919
1920 // cvr_w_returns is a speed check: Can we return one write
1921 // acknowledgement per clock cycle?
1922 initial cvr_w_returns = 0;
1923 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1924 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1925 cvr_w_returns = 0;
1926 else begin
1927 cvr_w_returns <= { cvr_w_returns[2:0], 1'b0 };
1928 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && S_AXI_BREADY[N] && !wgrant[N][NS])
1929 cvr_w_returns[0] <= 1'b1;
1930 end
1931
1932 initial cvr_whsreturn = 0;
1933 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1934 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1935 cvr_whsreturn <= 0;
1936 else
1937 cvr_whsreturn <= cvr_whsreturn || (&cvr_w_returns);
1938
1939 // w_every is a connectivity test: Can we get a return from
1940 // every slave?
1941 initial cvr_w_every = 0;
1942 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1943 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1944 cvr_w_every <= 0;
1945 else if (!S_AXI_AWVALID[N])
1946 cvr_w_every <= 0;
1947 else begin
1948 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && S_AXI_BREADY[N] && !wgrant[N][NS])
1949 cvr_w_every[swindex[N]] <= 1'b1;
1950 end
1951
1952 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1953 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N])
1954 assert($stable(swindex[N]));
1955
1956 initial cvr_was_wevery = 0;
1957 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1958 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1959 cvr_was_wevery <= 0;
1960 else
1961 cvr_was_wevery <= cvr_was_wevery || (&cvr_w_every);
1962
1963 // err_wr_return is a test to make certain we can return a
1964 // bus error on the write channel.
1965 initial err_wr_return = 0;
1966 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1967 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1968 err_wr_return = 0;
1969 else if (wgrant[N][NS] && S_AXI_BVALID[N]
1970 && (S_AXI_BRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR))
1971 err_wr_return = 1;
1972
1973`ifndef VERILATOR
1974 always @(*)
1975 cover(!swgrant[N] && cvr_whsreturn);
1976 always @(*)
1977 cover(!swgrant[N] && cvr_was_wevery);
1978
1979 always @(*)
1980 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && wrequest[N][NS]);
1981 always @(*)
1982 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && wrequest[N][NS] && slave_awaccepts[N]);
1983 always @(*)
1984 cover(err_wr_return);
1985 always @(*)
1986 cover(!swgrant[N] && err_wr_return);
1987`endif
1988
1989 always @(*)
1990 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N])
1991 assert(swgrant[N]);
1992
1993 // cvr_r_returns is a speed check: Can we return one read
1994 // acknowledgment per clock cycle?
1995 initial cvr_r_returns = 0;
1996 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
1997 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
1998 cvr_r_returns = 0;
1999 else begin
2000 cvr_r_returns <= { cvr_r_returns[2:0], 1'b0 };
2001 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && S_AXI_RREADY[N])
2002 cvr_r_returns[0] <= 1'b1;
2003 end
2004
2005 initial cvr_rhsreturn = 0;
2006 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2007 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2008 cvr_rhsreturn <= 0;
2009 else
2010 cvr_rhsreturn <= cvr_rhsreturn || (&cvr_r_returns);
2011
2012
2013 // r_every is a connectivity test: Can we get a read return from
2014 // every slave?
2015 initial cvr_r_every = 0;
2016 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2017 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2018 cvr_r_every = 0;
2019 else if (!S_AXI_ARVALID[N])
2020 cvr_r_every = 0;
2021 else begin
2022 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && S_AXI_RREADY[N])
2023 cvr_r_every[srindex[N]] <= 1'b1;
2024 end
2025
2026 // cvr_was_revery is a return to idle check following the
2027 // connectivity test. Since the connectivity test is cleared
2028 // if there's ever a drop in the valid line, we need a separate
2029 // wire to check that this master can return to idle again.
2030 initial cvr_was_revery = 0;
2031 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2032 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2033 cvr_was_revery <= 0;
2034 else
2035 cvr_was_revery <= cvr_was_revery || (&cvr_r_every);
2036
2037 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2038 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N])
2039 assert($stable(srindex[N]));
2040
2041 initial err_rd_return = 0;
2042 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2043 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2044 err_rd_return = 0;
2045 else if (rgrant[N][NS] && S_AXI_RVALID[N]
2046 && (S_AXI_RRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR))
2047 err_rd_return = 1;
2048
2049`ifndef VERILATOR
2050 always @(*)
2051 cover(!srgrant[N] && cvr_rhsreturn); // @26
2052 always @(*)
2053 cover(!srgrant[N] && cvr_was_revery); // @26
2054
2055 always @(*)
2056 cover(S_AXI_ARVALID[N] && rrequest[N][NS]);
2057 always @(*)
2058 cover(rgrant[N][NS]);
2059 always @(*)
2060 cover(err_rd_return);
2061 always @(*)
2062 cover(!srgrant[N] && err_rd_return); //@!
2063`endif
2064
2065 always @(*)
2066 if (S_AXI_BVALID[N] && wgrant[N][NS])
2067 assert(S_AXI_BRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR);
2068 always @(*)
2069 if (S_AXI_RVALID[N] && rgrant[N][NS])
2070 assert(S_AXI_RRESP[2*N+:2]==INTERCONNECT_ERROR);
2071 end endgenerate
2072
2073 reg cvr_multi_write_hit, cvr_multi_read_hit;
2074
2075 initial cvr_multi_write_hit = 0;
2076 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2077 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2078 cvr_multi_write_hit <= 0;
2079 else if (fm_awr_outstanding[0] > 2 && !wgrant[0][NS])
2080 cvr_multi_write_hit <= 1;
2081
2082 initial cvr_multi_read_hit = 0;
2083 always @(posedge S_AXI_ACLK)
2084 if (!S_AXI_ARESETN)
2085 cvr_multi_read_hit <= 0;
2086 else if (fm_rd_outstanding[0] > 2 && !rgrant[0][NS])
2087 cvr_multi_read_hit <= 1;
2088
2089 always @(*)
2090 cover(cvr_multi_write_hit);
2091
2092 always @(*)
2093 cover(cvr_multi_read_hit);
2094
2095 always @(*)
2096 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && cvr_multi_write_hit & mwgrant == 0 && M_AXI_BVALID == 0);
2097
2098 always @(*)
2099 cover(S_AXI_ARESETN && cvr_multi_read_hit & mrgrant == 0 && M_AXI_RVALID == 0);
2100 // }}}
2101 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2102 //
2103 // Negation check
2104 // {{{
2105 // Pick a particular value. Assume the value doesn't show up on the
2106 // input. Prove it doesn't show up on the output. This will check for
2107 // ...
2108 // 1. Stuck bits on the output channel
2109 // 2. Cross-talk between channels
2110 //
2111 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2112 //
2113 //
2114 (* anyconst *) reg [LGNM-1:0] f_const_source;
2115 (* anyconst *) reg [AW-1:0] f_const_addr;
2116 (* anyconst *) reg [AW-1:0] f_const_addr_n;
2117 (* anyconst *) reg [DW-1:0] f_const_data_n;
2118 (* anyconst *) reg [DW/8-1:0] f_const_strb_n;
2119 (* anyconst *) reg [3-1:0] f_const_prot_n;
2120 (* anyconst *) reg [2-1:0] f_const_resp_n;
2121 reg [LGNS-1:0] f_const_slave;
2122
2123 always @(*)
2124 assume(f_const_source < NM);
2125 always @(*)
2126 begin
2127 f_const_slave = NS;
2128 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
2129 begin
2130 if (((f_const_addr ^ SLAVE_ADDR[iM*AW+:AW])
2131 &SLAVE_MASK[iM*AW+:AW])==0)
2132 f_const_slave = iM;
2133 end
2134
2135 assume(f_const_slave < NS);
2136 end
2137
2138 reg [AW-1:0] f_awaddr;
2139 reg [AW-1:0] f_araddr;
2140 always @(*)
2141 f_awaddr = S_AXI_AWADDR[f_const_source * AW +: AW];
2142 always @(*)
2143 f_araddr = S_AXI_ARADDR[f_const_source * AW +: AW];
2144
2145 // The assumption check: assume our negated values are not found on
2146 // the inputs
2147 always @(*)
2148 begin
2149 if (S_AXI_AWVALID[f_const_source])
2150 begin
2151 assume(f_awaddr != f_const_addr_n);
2152 assume(S_AXI_AWPROT[f_const_source*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2153 end
2154 if (w_wvalid)
2155 begin
2156 assume(m_wdata[f_const_source] != f_const_data_n);
2157 assume(m_wstrb[f_const_source] != f_const_strb_n);
2158 end
2159 if (S_AXI_ARVALID[f_const_source])
2160 begin
2161 assume(f_araddr != f_const_addr_n);
2162 assume(S_AXI_ARPROT[f_const_source*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2163 end
2164
2165 if (M_AXI_BVALID[f_const_slave] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2166 begin
2167 assume(m_bresp[f_const_slave] != f_const_resp_n);
2168 end
2169
2170 if (M_AXI_RVALID[f_const_slave] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2171 begin
2172 assume(m_rdata[f_const_slave] != f_const_data_n);
2173 assume(m_rresp[f_const_slave] != f_const_resp_n);
2174 end
2175 end
2176
2177 // Proof check: Prove these values are not found on our outputs
2178 always @(*)
2179 begin
2180 if (skd_awvalid[f_const_source])
2181 begin
2182 assert(skd_awaddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2183 assert(skd_awprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2184 end
2185 if (dcd_awvalid[f_const_source])
2186 begin
2187 assert(m_awaddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2188 assert(m_awprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2189 end
2190 if (M_AXI_AWVALID[f_const_slave] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2191 begin
2192 assert(M_AXI_AWADDR[f_const_slave*AW+:AW] != f_const_addr_n);
2193 assert(M_AXI_AWPROT[f_const_slave*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2194 end
2195 if (M_AXI_WVALID[f_const_slave] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2196 begin
2197 assert(M_AXI_WDATA[f_const_slave*DW+:DW] != f_const_data_n);
2198 assert(M_AXI_WSTRB[f_const_slave*(DW/8)+:(DW/8)] != f_const_strb_n);
2199 end
2200 if (skd_arvalid[f_const_source])
2201 begin
2202 assert(skd_araddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2203 assert(skd_arprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2204 end
2205 if (dcd_arvalid[f_const_source])
2206 begin
2207 assert(w_araddr[f_const_source] != f_const_addr_n);
2208 assert(w_arprot[f_const_source] != f_const_prot_n);
2209 end
2210 if (M_AXI_ARVALID[f_const_slave] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2211 begin
2212 assert(M_AXI_ARADDR[f_const_slave*AW+:AW] != f_const_addr_n);
2213 assert(M_AXI_ARPROT[f_const_slave*3+:3] != f_const_prot_n);
2214 end
2215 //
2216 if (r_bvalid[f_const_source] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2217 assert(r_bresp[f_const_source] != f_const_resp_n);
2218 if (S_AXI_BVALID[f_const_source] && wgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2219 assert(S_AXI_BRESP[f_const_source*2+:2] != f_const_resp_n);
2220 if (r_rvalid[f_const_source] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2221 begin
2222 assert(r_rresp[f_const_source] != f_const_resp_n);
2223 assert(r_rdata[f_const_source] != f_const_data_n);
2224 end
2225 if (S_AXI_RVALID[f_const_source] && rgrant[f_const_source][f_const_slave])
2226 begin
2227 assert(S_AXI_RRESP[f_const_source*2+:2]!=f_const_resp_n);
2228 assert(S_AXI_RDATA[f_const_source*DW+:DW]!=f_const_data_n);
2229 end
2230 end
2231 // }}}
2232 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2233 //
2234 // (Careless) constraining assumptions
2235 // {{{
2236 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2237 //
2238 //
2239 generate for(N=0; N<NM; N=N+1)
2240 begin
2241
2242 end endgenerate
2243 // }}}
2244`endif
2245// }}}
2246endmodule
2247`ifndef YOSYS
2248`default_nettype wire
2249`endif
addrdecode.v

original/upstream/rtl/addrdecode.v

1////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2//
3// Filename: rtl/addrdecode.v
4// {{{
5// Project: WB2AXIPSP: bus bridges and other odds and ends
6//
7// Purpose: Supports bus crossbars by answering the question, which slave
8// does the current address need to be routed to? Requests are
9// pipelined using valid/!stall handshaking. For those familiar with
10// AXI, READY=!STALL. The outgoing stream is identical to the incoming
11// one, save for the (new) o_decode field. This is a bitmask containing
12// one bit for each slave that the request might be routed to, and one
13// extra bit to indicate no slaves matched.
14//
15// The keys to the operation of this module are found in the two
16// parameters, SLAVE_ADDR and SLAVE_MASK.
17//
18// SLAVE_ADDR specifies the address of the slave in question. It's a large
19// array, with one address (i.e. one set of AW bits) for each
20// potential slave address region.
21//
22// SLAVE_MASK specifies which of the bits in SLAVE_ADDR need to match in
23// order to route a request to a that slave.
24//
25// It's important to guarantee that no two slaves will ever map to the
26// same address, and likewise any given slave may only map to a single
27// address region.
28//
29// Incidentally, the algorithm forces all slaves to have an address
30// aligned with their memory size. Hence a 2GB memory must have an
31// address (range) of either 0-2GB, 2GB-4GB, 4GB-6GB, etc. However, a
32// second slave having only 8kB of memory may be placed at 0-8kB,
33// 8-16kB, 16-24kB, etc. For logic minimization purposes, it is often to
34// the advantage of the bus compositor to minimize the number of mask
35// bits, and hence 8kB slaves may be aliased to many places in memory.
36// Bus composition and address assignment, however, are both outside of
37// the scope of the operation of this module.
38//
39//
40// Creator: Dan Gisselquist, Ph.D.
41// Gisselquist Technology, LLC
42//
43////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
44// }}}
45// Copyright (C) 2019-2025, Gisselquist Technology, LLC
46// {{{
47// This file is part of the WB2AXIP project.
48//
49// The WB2AXIP project contains free software and gateware, licensed under the
50// Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"). You may not use this project,
51// or this file, except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy
52// of the License at
53// }}}
54// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
55// {{{
56// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
57// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT
58// WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. See the
59// License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations
60// under the License.
61//
62////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
63//
64`default_nettype none
65// }}}
66module addrdecode #(
67 // {{{
68 parameter NS=8,
69 parameter AW = 32, DW=32+32/8+1+1,
70 //
71 // SLAVE_ADDR contains address assignments for each of the
72 // various slaves we are adjudicating between.
73 parameter [NS*AW-1:0] SLAVE_ADDR = {
74 { 3'b111, {(AW-3){1'b0}} },
75 { 3'b110, {(AW-3){1'b0}} },
76 { 3'b101, {(AW-3){1'b0}} },
77 { 3'b100, {(AW-3){1'b0}} },
78 { 3'b011, {(AW-3){1'b0}} },
79 { 3'b010, {(AW-3){1'b0}} },
80 { 4'b0010, {(AW-4){1'b0}} },
81 { 4'b0000, {(AW-4){1'b0}} }},
82 //
83 // SLAVE_MASK contains a mask of those address bits in
84 // SLAVE_ADDR which are relevant. It shall be true that if
85 // !SLAVE_MASK[k] then !SLAVE_ADDR[k], for any bits of k
86 parameter [NS*AW-1:0] SLAVE_MASK = (NS <= 1) ? 0
87 : { {(NS-2){ 3'b111, {(AW-3){1'b0}} }},
88 {(2){ 4'b1111, {(AW-4){1'b0}} }} },
89 //
90 // ACCESS_ALLOWED is a bit-wise mask indicating which slaves
91 // may get access to the bus. If ACCESS_ALLOWED[slave] is true,
92 // then a master can connect to the slave via this method. This
93 // parameter is primarily here to support AXI (or other similar
94 // buses) which may have separate accesses for both read and
95 // write. By using this, a read-only slave can be connected,
96 // which would also naturally create an error on any attempt to
97 // write to it.
98 parameter [NS-1:0] ACCESS_ALLOWED = -1,
99 //
100 // If OPT_REGISTERED is set, address decoding will take an extra
101 // clock, and will register the results of the decoding
102 // operation.
103 parameter [0:0] OPT_REGISTERED = 0,
104 //
105 // If OPT_LOWPOWER is set, then whenever the output is not
106 // valid, any respective data linse will also be forced to zero
107 // in an effort to minimize power.
108 parameter [0:0] OPT_LOWPOWER = 0
109 // }}}
110 ) (
111 // {{{
112 input wire i_clk, i_reset,
113 //
114 input wire i_valid,
115 output reg o_stall,
116 input wire [AW-1:0] i_addr,
117 input wire [DW-1:0] i_data,
118 //
119 output reg o_valid,
120 input wire i_stall,
121 output reg [NS:0] o_decode,
122 output reg [AW-1:0] o_addr,
123 output reg [DW-1:0] o_data
124 // }}}
125 );
126
127 // Local declarations
128 // {{{
129 //
130 // OPT_NONESEL controls whether or not the address lines are fully
131 // proscribed, or whether or not a "no-slave identified" slave should
132 // be created. To avoid a "no-slave selected" output, slave zero must
133 // have no mask bits set (and therefore no address bits set), and it
134 // must also allow access.
135 localparam [0:0] OPT_NONESEL = (!ACCESS_ALLOWED[0])
136 || (SLAVE_MASK[AW-1:0] != 0);
137 //
138 wire [NS:0] request;
139 reg [NS-1:0] prerequest;
140 integer iM;
141 // }}}
142
143 // prerequest
144 // {{{
145 always @(*)
146 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
147 prerequest[iM] = (((i_addr ^ SLAVE_ADDR[iM*AW +: AW])
148 &SLAVE_MASK[iM*AW +: AW])==0)
149 &&(ACCESS_ALLOWED[iM]);
150 // }}}
151
152 // request
153 // {{{
154 generate if (OPT_NONESEL)
155 begin : NO_DEFAULT_REQUEST
156 // {{{
157 reg [NS-1:0] r_request;
158
159 // Need to create a slave to describe when nothing is selected
160 //
161 always @(*)
162 begin
163 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
164 r_request[iM] = i_valid && prerequest[iM];
165 if (!OPT_NONESEL && (NS > 1 && |prerequest[NS-1:1]))
166 r_request[0] = 1'b0;
167 end
168
169 assign request[NS-1:0] = r_request;
170 // }}}
171 end else if (NS == 1)
172 begin : SINGLE_SLAVE
173 // {{{
174 assign request[0] = i_valid;
175
176 // Verilator lint_off UNUSED
177 wire unused;
178 assign unused = &{ 1'b0, prerequest };
179 // Verilator lint_on UNUSED
180 // }}}
181 end else begin : GENERAL_CASE
182 // {{{
183 reg [NS-1:0] r_request;
184
185 always @(*)
186 begin
187 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
188 r_request[iM] = i_valid && prerequest[iM];
189 if (!OPT_NONESEL && (NS > 1 && |prerequest[NS-1:1]))
190 r_request[0] = 1'b0;
191 end
192
193 assign request[NS-1:0] = r_request;
194 // }}}
195 end endgenerate
196 // }}}
197
198 // request[NS]
199 // {{{
200 generate if (OPT_NONESEL)
201 begin : GENERATE_NONSEL_SLAVE
202 reg r_request_NS, r_none_sel;
203
204 always @(*)
205 begin
206 // Let's assume nothing's been selected, and then check
207 // to prove ourselves wrong.
208 //
209 // Note that none_sel will be considered an error
210 // condition in the follow-on processing. Therefore
211 // it's important to clear it if no request is pending.
212 r_none_sel = i_valid && (prerequest == 0);
213 //
214 // request[NS] indicates a request for a non-existent
215 // slave. A request that should (eventually) return a
216 // bus error
217 //
218 r_request_NS = r_none_sel;
219 end
220
221 assign request[NS] = r_request_NS;
222 end else begin : NO_NONESEL_SLAVE
223 assign request[NS] = 1'b0;
224 end endgenerate
225 // }}}
226
227 // o_valid, o_addr, o_data, o_decode, o_stall
228 // {{{
229 generate if (OPT_REGISTERED)
230 begin : GEN_REG_OUTPUTS
231
232 // o_valid
233 // {{{
234 initial o_valid = 0;
235 always @(posedge i_clk)
236 if (i_reset)
237 o_valid <= 0;
238 else if (!o_stall)
239 o_valid <= i_valid;
240 // }}}
241
242 // o_addr, o_data
243 // {{{
244 initial o_addr = 0;
245 initial o_data = 0;
246 always @(posedge i_clk)
247 if (i_reset && OPT_LOWPOWER)
248 begin
249 o_addr <= 0;
250 o_data <= 0;
251 end else if ((!o_valid || !i_stall)
252 && (i_valid || !OPT_LOWPOWER))
253 begin
254 o_addr <= i_addr;
255 o_data <= i_data;
256 end else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !i_stall)
257 begin
258 o_addr <= 0;
259 o_data <= 0;
260 end
261 // }}}
262
263 // o_decode
264 // {{{
265 initial o_decode = 0;
266 always @(posedge i_clk)
267 if (i_reset)
268 o_decode <= 0;
269 else if ((!o_valid || !i_stall)
270 && (i_valid || !OPT_LOWPOWER))
271 o_decode <= request;
272 else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && !i_stall)
273 o_decode <= 0;
274 // }}}
275
276 // o_stall
277 // {{{
278 always @(*)
279 o_stall = (o_valid && i_stall);
280 // }}}
281 end else begin : GEN_COMBINATORIAL_OUTPUTS
282
283 always @(*)
284 begin
285 o_valid = i_valid;
286 o_stall = i_stall;
287 o_addr = i_addr;
288 o_data = i_data;
289
290 o_decode = request;
291 end
292
293 // Make Verilator happy
294 // {{{
295 // verilator coverage_off
296 // verilator lint_off UNUSED
297 wire unused;
298 assign unused = &{ 1'b0,
299`ifdef VERILATOR
300 // Can't declare the clock as unused for formal,
301 // lest it not be recognized as *the* clock
302 i_clk,
303`endif
304 i_reset };
305 // verilator lint_on UNUSED
306 // verilator coverage_on
307 // }}}
308 end endgenerate
309 // }}}
310////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
311////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
312////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
313//
314// Formal properties
315// {{{
316////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
317////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
318////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
319`ifdef FORMAL
320 reg f_past_valid;
321 initial f_past_valid = 0;
322 always @(posedge i_clk)
323 f_past_valid <= 1;
324
325 reg [AW+DW-1:0] f_idata;
326 always @(*)
327 f_idata = { i_addr, i_data };
328
329`ifdef ADDRDECODE
330 always @(posedge i_clk)
331 if (!f_past_valid)
332 assume(i_reset);
333`else
334 always @(posedge i_clk)
335 if (!f_past_valid)
336 assert(i_reset);
337
338`endif // ADDRDECODE
339 always @(posedge i_clk)
340 if (OPT_REGISTERED && (!f_past_valid || $past(i_reset)))
341 begin
342 assert(!o_valid);
343 assert(o_decode == 0);
344 end else if ($past(o_valid && i_stall) && OPT_REGISTERED)
345 begin
346 assert($stable(o_addr));
347 assert($stable(o_decode));
348 assert($stable(o_data));
349 end
350
351 // If the output is ever valid, there must be at least one
352 // decoded output
353 always @(*)
354 assert(o_valid == (o_decode != 0));
355
356 always @(*)
357 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
358 if (o_decode[iM])
359 begin
360 // The address must match
361 assert((((o_addr ^ SLAVE_ADDR[iM*AW +: AW])
362 & SLAVE_MASK[iM*AW +: AW])==0)
363 && ACCESS_ALLOWED[iM]);
364 //
365 // And nothing else must match
366 assert(o_decode == (1<<iM));
367 end
368
369 always @(*)
370 for(iM=0; iM<NS; iM=iM+1)
371 if (!ACCESS_ALLOWED[iM])
372 assert(!o_decode[iM]);
373
374 // LOWPOWER check
375 // {{{
376 generate if (OPT_LOWPOWER && OPT_REGISTERED)
377 begin
378 always @(*)
379 if (!o_valid)
380 begin
381 assert(o_addr == 0);
382 assert(o_decode == 0);
383 assert(o_data == 0);
384 end
385 end endgenerate
386 // }}}
387
388 //
389 // The output decoded value may only ever have one value high,
390 // never more--i.e. $onehot0
391 // {{{
392`ifdef VERIFIC
393 always @(*)
394 assert($onehot0(request));
395`else
396 reg onehot_request;
397 always @(*)
398 begin
399 onehot_request = 0;
400 for(iM=0; iM<NS+1; iM=iM+1)
401 if ((request ^ (1<<iM))==0)
402 onehot_request = 1;
403 end
404
405 always @(*)
406 if (request != 0)
407 assert(onehot_request);
408`endif
409 // }}}
410
411 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
412 //
413 // Cover properties
414 // {{{
415 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
416 //
417 //
418
419 //
420 // Make sure all addresses are reachable
421 //
422 reg [NS:0] f_reached;
423
424 always @(posedge i_clk)
425 cover(i_valid);
426
427 always @(posedge i_clk)
428 cover(o_valid);
429
430 always @(posedge i_clk)
431 cover(o_valid && !i_stall);
432
433 initial f_reached = 0;
434 always @(posedge i_clk)
435 if (i_reset)
436 f_reached = 0;
437 else if (o_valid)
438 f_reached = f_reached | o_decode;
439
440 generate if (!OPT_NONESEL && ACCESS_ALLOWED[0]
441 && SLAVE_MASK == 0 && NS == 1)
442 begin
443
444 always @(*)
445 cover(f_reached[0]);
446
447 always @(posedge i_clk)
448 if (f_past_valid && $stable(o_valid))
449 assert($stable(o_decode));
450
451 end else begin
452
453 always @(*)
454 cover(&f_reached);
455
456 always @(posedge i_clk)
457 if (f_past_valid && $stable(o_valid))
458 cover($changed(o_decode));
459
460 end endgenerate
461 // }}}
462`endif // FORMAL
463// }}}
464endmodule
465`ifndef YOSYS
466`default_nettype wire
467`endif
skidbuffer.v

original/upstream/rtl/skidbuffer.v

1////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2//
3// Filename: rtl/skidbuffer.v
4// {{{
5// Project: WB2AXIPSP: bus bridges and other odds and ends
6//
7// Purpose: A basic SKID buffer.
8// {{{
9// Skid buffers are required for high throughput AXI code, since the AXI
10// specification requires that all outputs be registered. This means
11// that, if there are any stall conditions calculated, it will take a clock
12// cycle before the stall can be propagated up stream. This means that
13// the data will need to be buffered for a cycle until the stall signal
14// can make it to the output.
15//
16// Handling that buffer is the purpose of this core.
17//
18// On one end of this core, you have the i_valid and i_data inputs to
19// connect to your bus interface. There's also a registered o_ready
20// signal to signal stalls for the bus interface.
21//
22// The other end of the core has the same basic interface, but it isn't
23// registered. This allows you to interact with the bus interfaces
24// as though they were combinatorial logic, by interacting with this half
25// of the core.
26//
27// If at any time the incoming !stall signal, i_ready, signals a stall,
28// the incoming data is placed into a buffer. Internally, that buffer
29// is held in r_data with the r_valid flag used to indicate that valid
30// data is within it.
31// }}}
32// Parameters:
33// {{{
34// DW or data width
35// In order to make this core generic, the width of the data in the
36// skid buffer is parameterized
37//
38// OPT_LOWPOWER
39// Forces both o_data and r_data to zero if the respective *VALID
40// signal is also low. While this costs extra logic, it can also
41// be used to guarantee that any unused values aren't toggling and
42// therefore unnecessarily using power.
43//
44// This excess toggling can be particularly problematic if the
45// bus signals have a high fanout rate, or a long signal path
46// across an FPGA.
47//
48// OPT_OUTREG
49// Causes the outputs to be registered
50//
51// OPT_PASSTHROUGH
52// Turns the skid buffer into a passthrough. Used for formal
53// verification only.
54// }}}
55// Creator: Dan Gisselquist, Ph.D.
56// Gisselquist Technology, LLC
57//
58////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
59// }}}
60// Copyright (C) 2019-2025, Gisselquist Technology, LLC
61// {{{
62// This file is part of the WB2AXIP project.
63//
64// The WB2AXIP project contains free software and gateware, licensed under the
65// Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"). You may not use this project,
66// or this file, except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy
67// of the License at
68// }}}
69// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
70// {{{
71// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
72// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT
73// WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. See the
74// License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations
75// under the License.
76//
77////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
78//
79`default_nettype none
80// }}}
81module skidbuffer #(
82 // {{{
83 parameter [0:0] OPT_LOWPOWER = 0,
84 parameter [0:0] OPT_OUTREG = 1,
85 //
86 parameter [0:0] OPT_PASSTHROUGH = 0,
87 parameter DW = 8,
88 parameter [0:0] OPT_INITIAL = 1'b1
89 // }}}
90 ) (
91 // {{{
92 input wire i_clk, i_reset,
93 input wire i_valid,
94 output wire o_ready,
95 input wire [DW-1:0] i_data,
96 output wire o_valid,
97 input wire i_ready,
98 output reg [DW-1:0] o_data
99 // }}}
100 );
101
102 wire [DW-1:0] w_data;
103
104 generate if (OPT_PASSTHROUGH)
105 begin : PASSTHROUGH
106 // {{{
107 assign { o_valid, o_ready } = { i_valid, i_ready };
108
109 always @(*)
110 if (!i_valid && OPT_LOWPOWER)
111 o_data = 0;
112 else
113 o_data = i_data;
114
115 assign w_data = 0;
116
117 // Keep Verilator happy
118 // Verilator lint_off UNUSED
119 // {{{
120 wire unused_passthrough;
121 assign unused_passthrough = &{ 1'b0, i_clk, i_reset };
122 // }}}
123 // Verilator lint_on UNUSED
124 // }}}
125 end else begin : LOGIC
126 // We'll start with skid buffer itself
127 // {{{
128 reg r_valid;
129 reg [DW-1:0] r_data;
130
131 // r_valid
132 // {{{
133 initial if (OPT_INITIAL) r_valid = 0;
134 always @(posedge i_clk)
135 if (i_reset)
136 r_valid <= 0;
137 else if ((i_valid && o_ready) && (o_valid && !i_ready))
138 // We have incoming data, but the output is stalled
139 r_valid <= 1;
140 else if (i_ready)
141 r_valid <= 0;
142 // }}}
143
144 // r_data
145 // {{{
146 initial if (OPT_INITIAL) r_data = 0;
147 always @(posedge i_clk)
148 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && i_reset)
149 r_data <= 0;
150 else if (OPT_LOWPOWER && (!o_valid || i_ready))
151 r_data <= 0;
152 else if ((!OPT_LOWPOWER || !OPT_OUTREG || i_valid) && o_ready)
153 r_data <= i_data;
154
155 assign w_data = r_data;
156 // }}}
157
158 // o_ready
159 // {{{
160 assign o_ready = !r_valid;
161 // }}}
162
163 //
164 // And then move on to the output port
165 //
166 if (!OPT_OUTREG)
167 begin : NET_OUTPUT
168 // Outputs are combinatorially determined from inputs
169 // {{{
170 // o_valid
171 // {{{
172 assign o_valid = !i_reset && (i_valid || r_valid);
173 // }}}
174
175 // o_data
176 // {{{
177 always @(*)
178 if (r_valid)
179 o_data = r_data;
180 else if (!OPT_LOWPOWER || i_valid)
181 o_data = i_data;
182 else
183 o_data = 0;
184 // }}}
185 // }}}
186 end else begin : REG_OUTPUT
187 // Register our outputs
188 // {{{
189 // o_valid
190 // {{{
191 reg ro_valid;
192
193 initial if (OPT_INITIAL) ro_valid = 0;
194 always @(posedge i_clk)
195 if (i_reset)
196 ro_valid <= 0;
197 else if (!o_valid || i_ready)
198 ro_valid <= (i_valid || r_valid);
199
200 assign o_valid = ro_valid;
201 // }}}
202
203 // o_data
204 // {{{
205 initial if (OPT_INITIAL) o_data = 0;
206 always @(posedge i_clk)
207 if (OPT_LOWPOWER && i_reset)
208 o_data <= 0;
209 else if (!o_valid || i_ready)
210 begin
211
212 if (r_valid)
213 o_data <= r_data;
214 else if (!OPT_LOWPOWER || i_valid)
215 o_data <= i_data;
216 else
217 o_data <= 0;
218 end
219 // }}}
220
221 // }}}
222 end
223 // }}}
224 end endgenerate
225
226 // Keep Verilator happy
227 // {{{
228 // verilator coverage_off
229 // Verilator lint_off UNUSED
230 wire unused;
231 assign unused = &{ 1'b0, w_data };
232 // Verilator lint_on UNUSED
233 // verilator coverage_on
234 // }}}
235////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
236////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
237////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
238//
239// Formal properties
240// {{{
241////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
242////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
243////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
244`ifdef FORMAL
245`ifdef SKIDBUFFER
246`define ASSUME assume
247`else
248`define ASSUME assert
249`endif
250
251 reg f_past_valid;
252
253 initial f_past_valid = 0;
254 always @(posedge i_clk)
255 f_past_valid <= 1;
256
257 always @(*)
258 if (!f_past_valid)
259 assume(i_reset);
260
261 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
262 //
263 // Incoming stream properties / assumptions
264 // {{{
265 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
266 //
267 always @(posedge i_clk)
268 if (!f_past_valid)
269 begin
270 `ASSUME(!i_valid || !OPT_INITIAL);
271 end else if ($past(i_valid && !o_ready && !i_reset) && !i_reset)
272 `ASSUME(i_valid && $stable(i_data));
273
274`ifdef VERIFIC
275`define FORMAL_VERIFIC
276 // Reset properties
277 property RESET_CLEARS_IVALID;
278 @(posedge i_clk) i_reset |=> !i_valid;
279 endproperty
280
281 property IDATA_HELD_WHEN_NOT_READY;
282 @(posedge i_clk) disable iff (i_reset)
283 i_valid && !o_ready |=> i_valid && $stable(i_data);
284 endproperty
285
286`ifdef SKIDBUFFER
287 assume property (IDATA_HELD_WHEN_NOT_READY);
288`else
289 assert property (IDATA_HELD_WHEN_NOT_READY);
290`endif
291`endif
292 // }}}
293 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
294 //
295 // Outgoing stream properties / assumptions
296 // {{{
297 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
298 //
299
300 generate if (!OPT_PASSTHROUGH)
301 begin
302
303 always @(posedge i_clk)
304 if (!f_past_valid) // || $past(i_reset))
305 begin
306 // Following any reset, valid must be deasserted
307 assert(!o_valid || !OPT_INITIAL);
308 end else if ($past(o_valid && !i_ready && !i_reset) && !i_reset)
309 // Following any stall, valid must remain high and
310 // data must be preserved
311 assert(o_valid && $stable(o_data));
312
313 end endgenerate
314 // }}}
315 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
316 //
317 // Other properties
318 // {{{
319 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
320 //
321 //
322 generate if (!OPT_PASSTHROUGH)
323 begin
324 // Rule #1:
325 // If registered, then following any reset we should be
326 // ready for a new request
327 // {{{
328 always @(posedge i_clk)
329 if (f_past_valid && $past(OPT_OUTREG && i_reset))
330 assert(o_ready);
331 // }}}
332
333 // Rule #2:
334 // All incoming data must either go directly to the
335 // output port, or into the skid buffer
336 // {{{
337`ifndef VERIFIC
338 always @(posedge i_clk)
339 if (f_past_valid && !$past(i_reset) && $past(i_valid && o_ready
340 && (!OPT_OUTREG || o_valid) && !i_ready))
341 assert(!o_ready && w_data == $past(i_data));
342`else
343 assert property (@(posedge i_clk)
344 disable iff (i_reset)
345 (i_valid && o_ready
346 && (!OPT_OUTREG || o_valid) && !i_ready)
347 |=> (!o_ready && w_data == $past(i_data)));
348`endif
349 // }}}
350
351 // Rule #3:
352 // After the last transaction, o_valid should become idle
353 // {{{
354 if (!OPT_OUTREG)
355 begin
356 // {{{
357 always @(posedge i_clk)
358 if (f_past_valid && !$past(i_reset) && !i_reset
359 && $past(i_ready))
360 begin
361 assert(o_valid == i_valid);
362 assert(!i_valid || (o_data == i_data));
363 end
364 // }}}
365 end else begin
366 // {{{
367 always @(posedge i_clk)
368 if (f_past_valid && !$past(i_reset))
369 begin
370 if ($past(i_valid && o_ready))
371 assert(o_valid);
372
373 if ($past(!i_valid && o_ready && i_ready))
374 assert(!o_valid);
375 end
376 // }}}
377 end
378 // }}}
379
380 // Rule #4
381 // Same thing, but this time for o_ready
382 // {{{
383 always @(posedge i_clk)
384 if (f_past_valid && $past(!o_ready && i_ready))
385 assert(o_ready);
386 // }}}
387
388 // If OPT_LOWPOWER is set, o_data and w_data both need to be
389 // zero any time !o_valid or !r_valid respectively
390 // {{{
391 if (OPT_LOWPOWER)
392 begin
393 always @(*)
394 if ((OPT_OUTREG || !i_reset) && !o_valid)
395 assert(o_data == 0);
396
397 always @(*)
398 if (o_ready)
399 assert(w_data == 0);
400
401 end
402 // }}}
403 end endgenerate
404 // }}}
405
406 always @(posedge i_clk)
407 if (!OPT_PASSTHROUGH && !i_reset && !o_ready)
408 assert(o_valid);
409
410 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
411 //
412 // Cover checks
413 // {{{
414 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
415 //
416 //
417`ifdef SKIDBUFFER
418 generate if (!OPT_PASSTHROUGH)
419 begin
420 reg f_changed_data;
421
422 initial f_changed_data = 0;
423 always @(posedge i_clk)
424 if (i_reset)
425 f_changed_data <= 1;
426 else if (i_valid && $past(!i_valid || o_ready))
427 begin
428 if (i_data != $past(i_data + 1))
429 f_changed_data <= 0;
430 end else if (!i_valid && i_data != 0)
431 f_changed_data <= 0;
432
433
434`ifndef VERIFIC
435 reg [3:0] cvr_steps, cvr_hold;
436
437 always @(posedge i_clk)
438 if (i_reset)
439 begin
440 cvr_steps <= 0;
441 cvr_hold <= 0;
442 end else begin
443 cvr_steps <= cvr_steps + 1;
444 cvr_hold <= cvr_hold + 1;
445 case(cvr_steps)
446 0: if (o_valid || i_valid)
447 cvr_steps <= 0;
448 1: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
449 cvr_steps <= 0;
450 2: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
451 cvr_steps <= 0;
452 3: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
453 cvr_steps <= 0;
454 4: if (!i_valid || i_ready)
455 cvr_steps <= 0;
456 5: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
457 cvr_steps <= 0;
458 6: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
459 cvr_steps <= 0;
460 7: if (!i_valid || i_ready)
461 cvr_steps <= 0;
462 8: if (!i_valid || i_ready)
463 cvr_steps <= 0;
464 9: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
465 cvr_steps <= 0;
466 10: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
467 cvr_steps <= 0;
468 11: if (!i_valid || !i_ready)
469 cvr_steps <= 0;
470 12: begin
471 cvr_steps <= cvr_steps;
472 cover(!o_valid && !i_valid && f_changed_data);
473 if (!o_valid || !i_ready)
474 cvr_steps <= 0;
475 else
476 cvr_hold <= cvr_hold + 1;
477 end
478 default: assert(0);
479 endcase
480 end
481
482`else
483 // Cover test
484 cover property (@(posedge i_clk)
485 disable iff (i_reset)
486 (!o_valid && !i_valid)
487 ##1 i_valid && i_ready [*3]
488 ##1 i_valid && !i_ready
489 ##1 i_valid && i_ready [*2]
490 ##1 i_valid && !i_ready [*2]
491 ##1 i_valid && i_ready [*3]
492 // Wait for the design to clear
493 ##1 o_valid && i_ready [*0:5]
494 ##1 (!o_valid && !i_valid && f_changed_data));
495`endif
496 end endgenerate
497`endif // SKIDBUFFER
498 // }}}
499`endif
500// }}}
501endmodule

1////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
2//
3// Filename: bench/formal/faxil_slave.v
4// {{{
5// Project: WB2AXIPSP: bus bridges and other odds and ends
6//
7// Purpose:
8//
9// Creator: Dan Gisselquist, Ph.D.
10// Gisselquist Technology, LLC
11//
12////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
13// }}}
14// Copyright (C) 2018-2025, Gisselquist Technology, LLC
15// {{{

18// The WB2AXIP project contains free software and gateware, licensed under the
19// Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"). You may not use this project,
20// or this file, except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy
21// of the License at
22// }}}
23// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
24// {{{
25// Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
26// distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT

28// License for the specific language governing permissions and limitations
29// under the License.

32//
33`default_nettype none
34// }}}
35module faxil_slave #(
36 // {{{
37 parameter C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH = 32,// Fixed, width of the AXI R&W data
38 parameter C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH = 28,// AXI Address width (log wordsize)
39 // F_OPT_XILINX, Certain Xilinx cores impose additional rules upon AXI
40 // write transactions, limiting how far the write and write address
41 // can be apart. If F_OPT_XILINX is set, these rules will be applied
42 // here as well. See in-line for more details.
43 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_XILINX = 1'b0,
44 // F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY, if set, will assume the master is always idle on
45 // te read channel, allowing you to test/focus on the write interface
46 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY = 1'b0,
47 // F_OPT_READ_ONLY, if set, will assume the master is always idle on
48 // the write channel, while asserting that all of the associated returns
49 // and counters are zero
50 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_READ_ONLY = 1'b0,
51 // F_OPT_BRESP: Allow any type of write response. If set clear, then
52 // error responses are disallowed.
53 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_BRESP = 1'b1,
54 // F_OPT_RRESP, if cleared, will disallow error responses
55 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_RRESP = 1'b1,
56 // F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET, if set, will cause the design to *assume* the
57 // existence of a correct reset, rather than asserting it. It is
58 // appropriate anytime the reset logic is outside of the circuit being
59 // examined
60 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET = 1'b1,
61 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_NO_RESET = 1'b1,
62 //
63 // F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET is for those designs that will reset the channels
64 // using an asynchronous reset. In these cases, the stability
65 // properties only apply when the async reset is not asserted.
66 // Likewise, when F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET is set, the reset assertions are
67 // applied *on the same clock cycle*, in addition to one cycle later.
68 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET = 1'b0,
69 parameter F_OPT_COVER_BURST = 0,
70 // F_LGDEPTH is the number of bits necessary to count the maximum
71 // number of items in flight.
72 parameter F_LGDEPTH = 4,
73 // F_AXI_MAXWAIT is the maximum number of clock cycles the
74 // master should have to wait for a slave to raise its ready flag to
75 // accept a request. Set to zero for no limit.
76 parameter F_AXI_MAXWAIT = 12,
77 // F_AXI_MAXRSTALL is the maximum number of clock cycles the
78 // slave should have to wait with a return valid signal high, but
79 // while the master's return ready signal is low. Set to zero for no
80 // limit.
81 parameter F_AXI_MAXRSTALL= 12,
82 // F_AXI_MAXDELAY is the maximum number of clock cycles between request
83 // and response within the slave. Set this to zero for no limit.
84 parameter F_AXI_MAXDELAY = 12,
85 //
86 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_INITIAL = 1'b1,
87
88 //
89 localparam DW = C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH,
90 localparam AW = C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH
91 // }}}
92 ) (
93 // {{{
94 input wire i_clk, // System clock
95 input wire i_axi_reset_n,
96
97 // AXI write address channel signals
98 // {{{
99 input wire i_axi_awvalid,
100 input wire i_axi_awready,
101 input wire [AW-1:0] i_axi_awaddr, // Write address
102 input wire [2:0] i_axi_awprot, // Protection
103 // }}}
104 // AXI write data channel signals
105 // {{{
106 input wire i_axi_wvalid,
107 input wire i_axi_wready,
108 input wire [DW-1:0] i_axi_wdata, // Write data
109 input wire [DW/8-1:0] i_axi_wstrb, // Write strobes
110 // }}}
111 // AXI write response channel signals
112 // {{{
113 input wire i_axi_bvalid,
114 input wire i_axi_bready,
115 input wire [1:0] i_axi_bresp, // Wr response
116 // }}}
117 // AXI read address channel signals
118 // {{{
119 input wire i_axi_arvalid,
120 input wire i_axi_arready,
121 input wire [AW-1:0] i_axi_araddr, // Read address
122 input wire [2:0] i_axi_arprot, // Protection
123 // }}}
124 // AXI read data channel signals
125 // {{{
126 input wire i_axi_rvalid,
127 input wire i_axi_rready,
128 input wire [DW-1:0] i_axi_rdata, // Read data
129 input wire [1:0] i_axi_rresp, // Read response
130 // }}}
131 output reg [(F_LGDEPTH-1):0] f_axi_rd_outstanding,
132 output reg [(F_LGDEPTH-1):0] f_axi_wr_outstanding,
133 output reg [(F_LGDEPTH-1):0] f_axi_awr_outstanding
134 // }}}
135 );
136
137 localparam MAX_SLAVE_TIMEOUT = (F_AXI_MAXWAIT > F_AXI_MAXDELAY)
138 ? (F_AXI_MAXWAIT) : F_AXI_MAXDELAY;
139 localparam MAX_TIMEOUT = (F_AXI_MAXRSTALL>MAX_SLAVE_TIMEOUT)
140 ? (F_AXI_MAXRSTALL) : MAX_SLAVE_TIMEOUT;
141 localparam LGTIMEOUT = $clog2(MAX_TIMEOUT+1);
142
143//*****************************************************************************
144// Parameter declarations
145//*****************************************************************************
146
147//*****************************************************************************
148// Internal register and wire declarations
149//*****************************************************************************
150
151 // wire w_fifo_full;
152 wire axi_rd_ack, axi_wr_ack, axi_ard_req, axi_awr_req, axi_wr_req;
153 // axi_rd_err, axi_wr_err;
154 reg f_past_valid;
155 reg [3:0] f_reset_length;
156 // integer k;
157
158 assign axi_ard_req = (i_axi_arvalid)&&(i_axi_arready) && i_axi_reset_n;
159 assign axi_awr_req = (i_axi_awvalid)&&(i_axi_awready) && i_axi_reset_n;
160 assign axi_wr_req = (i_axi_wvalid )&&(i_axi_wready) && i_axi_reset_n;
161 //
162 assign axi_rd_ack = (i_axi_rvalid)&&(i_axi_rready) && i_axi_reset_n;
163 assign axi_wr_ack = (i_axi_bvalid)&&(i_axi_bready) && i_axi_reset_n;
164 // assign axi_rd_err = (axi_rd_ack)&&(i_axi_rresp[1]) && i_axi_reset_n;
165 // assign axi_wr_err = (axi_wr_ack)&&(i_axi_bresp[1]) && i_axi_reset_n;
166
167`define SLAVE_ASSUME assume
168`define SLAVE_ASSERT assert
169
170 //
171 // Setup
172 //
173
174 initial f_past_valid = 1'b0;
175 always @(posedge i_clk)
176 f_past_valid <= 1'b1;
177
178 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
179 //
180 // Reset properties
181 // {{{
182 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
183 //
184 //
185
186 //
187 // Insist that the reset signal start out asserted (negative), and
188 // remain so for 16 clocks.
189 //
190
191 generate if (F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET)
192 begin : ASSUME_INITIAL_RESET
193 always @(*)
194 if (!f_past_valid)
195 assume(!i_axi_reset_n);
196 end else begin : ASSERT_INITIAL_RESET
197 always @(*)
198 if (!f_past_valid)
199 assert(!i_axi_reset_n);
200 end endgenerate
201
202
203 //
204 // If asserted, the reset must be asserted for a minimum of 16 clocks
205 initial f_reset_length = 0;
206 always @(posedge i_clk)
207 if (F_OPT_NO_RESET || i_axi_reset_n)
208 f_reset_length <= 0;
209 else if (!(&f_reset_length))
210 f_reset_length <= f_reset_length + 1'b1;
211
212
213 //
214 // If the reset is not generated within this particular core, then it
215 // can be assumed if F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET is set
216 generate if (F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET && !F_OPT_NO_RESET)
217 begin : ASSUME_RESET
218 always @(posedge i_clk)
219 if ((f_past_valid)&&(!$past(i_axi_reset_n))&&(!$past(&f_reset_length)))
220 assume(!i_axi_reset_n);
221
222 always @(*)
223 if ((f_reset_length > 0)&&(f_reset_length < 4'hf))
224 assume(!i_axi_reset_n);
225
226 end else if (!F_OPT_NO_RESET)
227 begin : ASSERT_RESET
228
229 always @(posedge i_clk)
230 if ((f_past_valid)&&(!$past(i_axi_reset_n))&&(!$past(&f_reset_length)))
231 assert(!i_axi_reset_n);
232
233 always @(*)
234 if ((f_reset_length > 0)&&(f_reset_length < 4'hf))
235 assert(!i_axi_reset_n);
236
237 end endgenerate
238
239 //
240 // All of the xVALID signals *MUST* be set low on the clock following
241 // a reset. Not in the spec, but also checked here is that they must
242 // also be set low initially.
243 always @(posedge i_clk)
244 if ((!f_past_valid && F_OPT_INITIAL)
245 ||(f_past_valid && !$past(i_axi_reset_n)))
246 begin
247 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_arvalid);
248 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_awvalid);
249 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_wvalid);
250 //
251 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_bvalid);
252 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_rvalid);
253 end
254
255 generate if (F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET)
256 begin
257 always @(*)
258 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
259 begin
260 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_arvalid);
261 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_awvalid);
262 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_wvalid);
263 //
264 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_bvalid);
265 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_rvalid);
266 end
267 end endgenerate
268 // }}}
269 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
270 //
271 // xRESP checking
272 // {{{
273 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
274
275 always @(*)
276 if ((i_axi_bvalid)&&(!F_OPT_BRESP)&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
277 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bresp == 0);
278 always @(*)
279 if ((i_axi_rvalid)&&(!F_OPT_RRESP)&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
280 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rresp == 0);
281 always @(*)
282 if (i_axi_bvalid&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
283 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bresp != 2'b01); // Exclusive access not allowed
284 always @(*)
285 if (i_axi_rvalid&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
286 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rresp != 2'b01); // Exclusive access not allowed
287
288 // }}}
289 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
290 //
291 // Stability properties--what happens if valid and not ready
292 // {{{
293 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
294 //
295 //
296
297 // Assume any response from the bus will not change prior to that
298 // response being accepted
299 always @(posedge i_clk)
300 if ((f_past_valid)&&($past(i_axi_reset_n))
301 &&(!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
302 begin
303 // Write address channel
304 if ((f_past_valid)&&($past(i_axi_awvalid && !i_axi_awready)))
305 begin
306 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_awvalid);
307 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_awaddr));
308 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_awprot));
309 end
310
311 // Write data channel
312 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
313 &&($past(i_axi_wvalid && !i_axi_wready)))
314 begin
315 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
316 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_wstrb));
317 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_wdata));
318 end
319
320 // Incoming Read address channel
321 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
322 &&($past(i_axi_arvalid && !i_axi_arready)))
323 begin
324 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_arvalid);
325 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_araddr));
326 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_arprot));
327 end
328
329 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
330 &&($past(i_axi_rvalid && !i_axi_rready)))
331 begin
332 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rvalid);
333 `SLAVE_ASSERT($stable(i_axi_rresp));
334 `SLAVE_ASSERT($stable(i_axi_rdata));
335 end
336
337 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
338 &&($past(i_axi_bvalid && !i_axi_bready)))
339 begin
340 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bvalid);
341 `SLAVE_ASSERT($stable(i_axi_bresp));
342 end
343 end
344
345 // Nothing should be returned or requested on the first clock
346 generate if (F_OPT_INITIAL)
347 begin : INITIAL_VALUE_CHECKS
348 initial `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_arvalid);
349 initial `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_awvalid);
350 initial `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_wvalid);
351 //
352 initial `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_bvalid);
353 initial `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_rvalid);
354 end endgenerate
355 // }}}
356 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
357 //
358 //
359 // Insist upon a maximum delay before a request is accepted
360 //
361 //
362 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
363 //
364 generate if (F_AXI_MAXWAIT > 0)
365 begin : CHECK_STALL_COUNT
366 reg [LGTIMEOUT-1:0] f_axi_awstall,
367 f_axi_wstall,
368 f_axi_arstall;
369
370 //
371 // AXI write address channel
372 //
373 // Count the number of times AWVALID is true while AWREADY
374 // is false. These are stalls, and we want to insist on a
375 // minimum number of them. However, if BVALID && !BREADY,
376 // then there's a reason for not accepting anything more.
377 // Similarly, many cores will only ever accept one request
378 // at a time, hence we won't count things as stalls if
379 // WR-PENDING > 0.
380 initial f_axi_awstall = 0;
381 always @(posedge i_clk)
382 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_awvalid)||(i_axi_awready)
383 ||(i_axi_bvalid))
384 f_axi_awstall <= 0;
385 else if ((f_axi_awr_outstanding >= f_axi_wr_outstanding)
386 &&(i_axi_awvalid && !i_axi_wvalid))
387 // If we are waiting for the write channel to be valid
388 // then don't count stalls
389 f_axi_awstall <= 0;
390 else
391 f_axi_awstall <= f_axi_awstall + 1'b1;
392
393 always @(*)
394 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_awstall < F_AXI_MAXWAIT);
395
396 //
397 // AXI write data channel
398 //
399 // Count the number of clock cycles that the write data
400 // channel is stalled, that is while WVALID && !WREADY.
401 // Since things can back up if BVALID & !BREADY, we avoid
402 // counting clock cycles in that circumstance
403 initial f_axi_wstall = 0;
404 always @(posedge i_clk)
405 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_wvalid)||(i_axi_wready)
406 ||(i_axi_bvalid))
407 f_axi_wstall <= 0;
408 else if ((f_axi_wr_outstanding >= f_axi_awr_outstanding)
409 &&(!i_axi_awvalid && i_axi_wvalid))
410 // If we are waiting for the write address channel
411 // to be valid, then don't count stalls
412 f_axi_wstall <= 0;
413 else
414 f_axi_wstall <= f_axi_wstall + 1'b1;
415
416 always @(*)
417 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wstall < F_AXI_MAXWAIT);
418
419 //
420 // AXI read address channel
421 //
422 // Similar to the first two above, once the master raises
423 // ARVALID, insist that the slave respond within a minimum
424 // number of clock cycles. Exceptions include any time
425 // RVALID is true, since that can back up the whole system,
426 // and any time the number of bursts is greater than zero,
427 // since many slaves can only accept one request at a time.
428 initial f_axi_arstall = 0;
429 always @(posedge i_clk)
430 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_arvalid)||(i_axi_arready)
431 ||(i_axi_rvalid))
432 f_axi_arstall <= 0;
433 else
434 f_axi_arstall <= f_axi_arstall + 1'b1;
435
436 always @(*)
437 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_arstall < F_AXI_MAXWAIT);
438
439 end endgenerate
440
441 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
442 //
443 //
444 // Insist upon a maximum delay before any response is accepted
445 //
446 // These are separate from the earlier ones, in case you wish to
447 // control them separately. For example, an interconnect might be
448 // forced to let a channel wait indefinitely for access, but it might
449 // not be appropriate to require the response to be able to wait
450 // indefinitely as well
451 //
452 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
453 //
454 generate if (F_AXI_MAXRSTALL > 0)
455 begin : CHECK_RESPONSE_STALLS
456 reg [LGTIMEOUT-1:0] f_axi_bstall,
457 f_axi_rstall;
458
459 // AXI write response channel
460 //
461 // Insist on a maximum number of clocks that BVALID can be
462 // high while BREADY is low
463 initial f_axi_bstall = 0;
464 always @(posedge i_clk)
465 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_bvalid)||(i_axi_bready))
466 f_axi_bstall <= 0;
467 else
468 f_axi_bstall <= f_axi_bstall + 1'b1;
469
470 always @(*)
471 `SLAVE_ASSUME(f_axi_bstall < F_AXI_MAXRSTALL);
472
473 // AXI read response channel
474 //
475 // Insist on a maximum number of clocks that RVALID can be
476 // high while RREADY is low
477 initial f_axi_rstall = 0;
478 always @(posedge i_clk)
479 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_rvalid)||(i_axi_rready))
480 f_axi_rstall <= 0;
481 else
482 f_axi_rstall <= f_axi_rstall + 1'b1;
483
484 always @(*)
485 `SLAVE_ASSUME(f_axi_rstall < F_AXI_MAXRSTALL);
486
487 end endgenerate
488
489 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
490 //
491 //
492 // Xilinx extensions/guarantees to the AXI protocol
493 //
494 // 1. The address line will never be more than two clocks ahead of
495 // the write data channel, and
496 // 2. The write data channel will never be more than one clock
497 // ahead of the address channel.
498 //
499 //
500 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
501 //
502 //
503 generate if (F_OPT_XILINX)
504 begin
505 // Rule number one:
506 always @(posedge i_clk)
507 if ((i_axi_reset_n)&&($past(i_axi_reset_n))
508 &&($past(i_axi_awvalid && !i_axi_wvalid,2))
509 &&($past(f_axi_awr_outstanding>=f_axi_wr_outstanding,2))
510 &&(!$past(i_axi_wvalid)))
511 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
512
513 always @(posedge i_clk)
514 if ((i_axi_reset_n)
515 &&(f_axi_awr_outstanding > 1)
516 &&(f_axi_awr_outstanding-1 > f_axi_wr_outstanding))
517 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
518
519 always @(posedge i_clk)
520 if ((i_axi_reset_n)
521 &&($past(f_axi_awr_outstanding > f_axi_wr_outstanding))
522 &&(!$past(axi_wr_req)))
523 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
524
525
526 // Rule number two:
527 always @(posedge i_clk)
528 if ((i_axi_reset_n)&&(f_axi_awr_outstanding < f_axi_wr_outstanding))
529 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_awvalid);
530 end endgenerate
531
532 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
533 //
534 //
535 // Count outstanding transactions. With these measures, we count
536 // once per any burst.
537 //
538 //
539 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
540 //
541 //
542
543 //
544 // Count outstanding write address channel requests
545 initial f_axi_awr_outstanding = 0;
546 always @(posedge i_clk)
547 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
548 f_axi_awr_outstanding <= 0;
549 else case({ (axi_awr_req), (axi_wr_ack) })
550 2'b10: f_axi_awr_outstanding <= f_axi_awr_outstanding + 1'b1;
551 2'b01: f_axi_awr_outstanding <= f_axi_awr_outstanding - 1'b1;
552 default: begin end
553 endcase
554
555 //
556 // Count outstanding write data channel requests
557 initial f_axi_wr_outstanding = 0;
558 always @(posedge i_clk)
559 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
560 f_axi_wr_outstanding <= 0;
561 else case({ (axi_wr_req), (axi_wr_ack) })
562 2'b01: f_axi_wr_outstanding <= f_axi_wr_outstanding - 1'b1;
563 2'b10: f_axi_wr_outstanding <= f_axi_wr_outstanding + 1'b1;
564 default: begin end
565 endcase
566
567 //
568 // Count outstanding read requests
569 initial f_axi_rd_outstanding = 0;
570 always @(posedge i_clk)
571 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
572 f_axi_rd_outstanding <= 0;
573 else case({ (axi_ard_req), (axi_rd_ack) })
574 2'b01: f_axi_rd_outstanding <= f_axi_rd_outstanding - 1'b1;
575 2'b10: f_axi_rd_outstanding <= f_axi_rd_outstanding + 1'b1;
576 default: begin end
577 endcase
578
579 //
580 // Do not let the number of outstanding requests overflow
581 always @(posedge i_clk)
582 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wr_outstanding < {(F_LGDEPTH){1'b1}});
583 always @(posedge i_clk)
584 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_awr_outstanding < {(F_LGDEPTH){1'b1}});
585 always @(posedge i_clk)
586 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_rd_outstanding < {(F_LGDEPTH){1'b1}});
587
588 //
589 // That means that requests need to stop when we're almost full
590 always @(posedge i_clk)
591 if ((F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n) && f_axi_awr_outstanding == { {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b1}}, 1'b0} )
592 assert(!i_axi_awready);
593 always @(posedge i_clk)
594 if ((F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n) && f_axi_wr_outstanding == { {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b1}}, 1'b0} )
595 assert(!i_axi_wready);
596 always @(posedge i_clk)
597 if ((F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n) && f_axi_rd_outstanding == { {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b1}}, 1'b0} )
598 assert(!i_axi_arready);
599
600 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
601 //
602 //
603 // Insist that all responses are returned in less than a maximum delay
604 // In this case, we count responses within a burst, rather than entire
605 // bursts.
606 //
607 //
608 // A unique feature to the backpressure mechanism within AXI is that
609 // we have to reset our delay counters in the case of any push back,
610 // since the response can't move forward if the master isn't (yet)
611 // ready for it.
612 //
613 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
614 generate if (F_AXI_MAXDELAY > 0)
615 begin : CHECK_MAX_DELAY
616
617 reg [LGTIMEOUT-1:0] f_axi_wr_ack_delay,
618 f_axi_rd_ack_delay;
619
620 //
621 // Count the clock cycles a write request (address + data) has
622 // been outstanding and without any response
623 initial f_axi_wr_ack_delay = 0;
624 always @(posedge i_clk)
625 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(i_axi_bvalid)
626 ||(f_axi_awr_outstanding==0)
627 ||(f_axi_wr_outstanding==0))
628 f_axi_wr_ack_delay <= 0;
629 else if (f_axi_wr_outstanding > 0)
630 f_axi_wr_ack_delay <= f_axi_wr_ack_delay + 1'b1;
631
632 //
633 // Count the clock cycles that any read request has been
634 // outstanding, but without any response.
635 initial f_axi_rd_ack_delay = 0;
636 always @(posedge i_clk)
637 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(i_axi_rvalid)||(f_axi_rd_outstanding==0))
638 f_axi_rd_ack_delay <= 0;
639 else
640 f_axi_rd_ack_delay <= f_axi_rd_ack_delay + 1'b1;
641
642
643 //
644 // Assert that write responses will be returned in a timely
645 // fashion
646 always @(*)
647 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wr_ack_delay < F_AXI_MAXDELAY);
648
649 //
650 // Assert that read responses will be returned in a timely
651 // fashion
652 always @(*)
653 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_rd_ack_delay < F_AXI_MAXDELAY);
654
655 end endgenerate
656
657 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
658 //
659 //
660 // Assume acknowledgements must follow requests
661 //
662 // The f_axi*outstanding counters count the number of requests. No
663 // acknowledgment should issue without a pending request
664 // burst. Further, the spec is clear: you can't acknowledge something
665 // on the same clock you get the request. There must be at least one
666 // clock delay.
667 //
668 //
669 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
670
671 //
672 // AXI write response channel
673 //
674 always @(posedge i_clk)
675 if (i_axi_bvalid && (F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
676 begin
677 // No BVALID w/o an outstanding request
678 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_awr_outstanding > 0);
679 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wr_outstanding > 0);
680 end
681
682 //
683 // AXI read data channel signals
684 //
685 always @(posedge i_clk)
686 if (i_axi_rvalid && (F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
687 // No RVALID w/o an outstanding request
688 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_rd_outstanding > 0);
689
690 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
691 //
692 //
693 // F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY or F_OPT_READ_ONLY
694 //
695 // Optionally disable either read or write channels (or both??)
696 //
697 //
698 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
699 //
700 //
701 initial assert((!F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY)||(!F_OPT_READ_ONLY));
702
703 generate if (F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY)
704 begin : NO_READS
705
706 // If there are no read requests (assumed), there should be
707 // no read responses
708 always @(*)
709 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_arvalid == 0);
710 always @(*)
711 assert(f_axi_rd_outstanding == 0);
712 always @(*)
713 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rvalid == 0);
714
715 end endgenerate
716
717 generate if (F_OPT_READ_ONLY)
718 begin : NO_WRITES
719
720 // If there are no write requests (assumed, address or data),
721 // there should be no read responses
722 always @(*)
723 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_awvalid == 0);
724 always @(*)
725 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid == 0);
726 always @(*)
727 assert(f_axi_wr_outstanding == 0);
728 always @(*)
729 assert(f_axi_awr_outstanding == 0);
730 always @(*)
731 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bvalid == 0);
732
733 end endgenerate
734
735 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
736 //
737 //
738 // Cover properties
739 //
740 // We'll use this to prove that transactions are even possible, and
741 // hence that we haven't so constrained the bus that nothing can take
742 // place.
743 //
744 //
745 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
746
747 //
748 // AXI write response channel
749 //
750 generate if (!F_OPT_READ_ONLY)
751 begin
752 always @(posedge i_clk)
753 // Make sure we can get a write acknowledgment
754 cover((i_axi_bvalid)&&(i_axi_bready));
755 end endgenerate
756
757 //
758 // AXI read response channel
759 //
760 generate if (!F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY)
761 begin
762 always @(posedge i_clk)
763 // Make sure we can get a response from the read channel
764 cover((i_axi_rvalid)&&(i_axi_rready));
765 end endgenerate
766
767 generate if (!F_OPT_READ_ONLY && F_OPT_COVER_BURST > 0)
768 begin : COVER_WRITE_BURSTS
769
770 reg [31:0] cvr_writes;
771
772 initial cvr_writes = 0;
773 always @(posedge i_clk)
774 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
775 cvr_writes <= 0;
776 else if (i_axi_bvalid && i_axi_bready && i_axi_bresp == 2'b00
777 && !(&cvr_writes))
778 cvr_writes <= cvr_writes + 1;
779
780 always @(*)
781 cover(cvr_writes == F_OPT_COVER_BURST);
782
783 end endgenerate
784
785 generate if (!F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY && F_OPT_COVER_BURST > 0)
786 begin : COVER_READ_BURSTS
787
788 reg [31:0] cvr_reads;
789
790 initial cvr_reads = 0;
791 always @(posedge i_clk)
792 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
793 cvr_reads <= 0;
794 else if (i_axi_rvalid && i_axi_rready && i_axi_rresp == 2'b00
795 && !(&cvr_reads))
796 cvr_reads <= cvr_reads + 1;
797
798 always @(*)
799 cover(cvr_reads == F_OPT_COVER_BURST);
800
801 end endgenerate
802
803`undef SLAVE_ASSUME
804`undef SLAVE_ASSERT
805endmodule
faxil_master.v
