35module faxil_master #(
36 // {{{
37 parameter C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH = 32,// Fixed, width of the AXI R&W data
38 parameter C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH = 28,// AXI Address width (log wordsize)
39 // F_OPT_XILINX, Certain Xilinx cores impose additional rules upon AXI
40 // write transactions, limiting how far the write and write address
41 // can be apart. If F_OPT_XILINX is set, these rules will be applied
42 // here as well. See in-line for more details.
43 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_XILINX = 1'b0,
44 // F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY, if set, will assume the master is always idle on
45 // te read channel, allowing you to test/focus on the write interface
46 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY = 1'b0,
47 // F_OPT_READ_ONLY, if set, will assume the master is always idle on
48 // the write channel, while asserting that all of the associated returns
49 // and counters are zero
50 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_READ_ONLY = 1'b0,
51 // F_OPT_BRESP: Allow any type of write response. If set clear, then
52 // error responses are disallowed.
53 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_BRESP = 1'b1,
54 // F_OPT_RRESP, if cleared, will disallow error responses
55 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_RRESP = 1'b1,
56 // F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET, if set, will cause the design to *assume* the
57 // existence of a correct reset, rather than asserting it. It is
58 // appropriate anytime the reset logic is outside of the circuit being
59 // examined
60 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET = 1'b0,
61 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_NO_RESET = F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET,
62 //
63 // F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET is for those designs that will reset the channels
64 // using an asynchronous reset. In these cases, the stability
65 // properties only apply when the async reset is not asserted.
66 // Likewise, when F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET is set, the reset assertions are
67 // applied *on the same clock cycle*, in addition to one cycle later.
68 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET = 1'b0,
69 parameter F_OPT_COVER_BURST = 0,
70 // F_LGDEPTH is the number of bits necessary to count the maximum
71 // number of items in flight.
72 parameter F_LGDEPTH = 4,
73 // F_AXI_MAXWAIT is the maximum number of clock cycles the
74 // master should have to wait for a slave to raise its ready flag to
75 // accept a request. Set to zero for no limit.
76 parameter F_AXI_MAXWAIT = 12,
77 // F_AXI_MAXRSTALL is the maximum number of clock cycles the
78 // slave should have to wait with a return valid signal high, but
79 // while the master's return ready signal is low. Set to zero for no
80 // limit.
81 parameter F_AXI_MAXRSTALL= 12,
82 // F_AXI_MAXDELAY is the maximum number of clock cycles between request
83 // and response within the slave. Set this to zero for no limit.
84 parameter F_AXI_MAXDELAY = 12,
85 //
86 parameter [0:0] F_OPT_INITIAL = 1'b1,
87
88 //
89 localparam DW = C_AXI_DATA_WIDTH,
90 localparam AW = C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH
91 // }}}
92 ) (
93 // {{{
94 input wire i_clk, // System clock
95 input wire i_axi_reset_n,
96
97 // AXI write address channel signals
98 // {{{
99 input wire i_axi_awvalid,
100 input wire i_axi_awready,
101 input wire [AW-1:0] i_axi_awaddr, // Write address
102 input wire [2:0] i_axi_awprot, // Protection
103 // }}}
104 // AXI write data channel signals
105 // {{{
106 input wire i_axi_wvalid,
107 input wire i_axi_wready,
108 input wire [DW-1:0] i_axi_wdata, // Write data
109 input wire [DW/8-1:0] i_axi_wstrb, // Write strobes
110 // }}}
111 // AXI write response channel signals
112 // {{{
113 input wire i_axi_bvalid,
114 input wire i_axi_bready,
115 input wire [1:0] i_axi_bresp, // Wr response
116 // }}}
117 // AXI read address channel signals
118 // {{{
119 input wire i_axi_arvalid,
120 input wire i_axi_arready,
121 input wire [AW-1:0] i_axi_araddr, // Read address
122 input wire [2:0] i_axi_arprot, // Protection
123 // }}}
124 // AXI read data channel signals
125 // {{{
126 input wire i_axi_rvalid,
127 input wire i_axi_rready,
128 input wire [DW-1:0] i_axi_rdata, // Read data
129 input wire [1:0] i_axi_rresp, // Read response
130 // }}}
131 output reg [(F_LGDEPTH-1):0] f_axi_rd_outstanding,
132 output reg [(F_LGDEPTH-1):0] f_axi_wr_outstanding,
133 output reg [(F_LGDEPTH-1):0] f_axi_awr_outstanding
134 // }}}
135 );
136
137 localparam MAX_SLAVE_TIMEOUT = (F_AXI_MAXWAIT > F_AXI_MAXDELAY)
138 ? (F_AXI_MAXWAIT) : F_AXI_MAXDELAY;
139 localparam MAX_TIMEOUT = (F_AXI_MAXRSTALL>MAX_SLAVE_TIMEOUT)
140 ? (F_AXI_MAXRSTALL) : MAX_SLAVE_TIMEOUT;
141 localparam LGTIMEOUT = $clog2(MAX_TIMEOUT+1);
142
143//*****************************************************************************
144// Parameter declarations
145//*****************************************************************************
146
147//*****************************************************************************
148// Internal register and wire declarations
149//*****************************************************************************
150
151 // wire w_fifo_full;
152 wire axi_rd_ack, axi_wr_ack, axi_ard_req, axi_awr_req, axi_wr_req;
153 // axi_rd_err, axi_wr_err;
154 reg f_past_valid;
155 reg [3:0] f_reset_length;
156 // integer k;
157
158 assign axi_ard_req = (i_axi_arvalid)&&(i_axi_arready) && i_axi_reset_n;
159 assign axi_awr_req = (i_axi_awvalid)&&(i_axi_awready) && i_axi_reset_n;
160 assign axi_wr_req = (i_axi_wvalid )&&(i_axi_wready) && i_axi_reset_n;
161 //
162 assign axi_rd_ack = (i_axi_rvalid)&&(i_axi_rready) && i_axi_reset_n;
163 assign axi_wr_ack = (i_axi_bvalid)&&(i_axi_bready) && i_axi_reset_n;
164 // assign axi_rd_err = (axi_rd_ack)&&(i_axi_rresp[1]) && i_axi_reset_n;
165 // assign axi_wr_err = (axi_wr_ack)&&(i_axi_bresp[1]) && i_axi_reset_n;
166
167`define SLAVE_ASSUME assert
168`define SLAVE_ASSERT assume
169
170 //
171 // Setup
172 //
173
174 initial f_past_valid = 1'b0;
175 always @(posedge i_clk)
176 f_past_valid <= 1'b1;
177
178 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
179 //
180 // Reset properties
181 // {{{
182 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
183 //
184 //
185
186 //
187 // Insist that the reset signal start out asserted (negative), and
188 // remain so for 16 clocks.
189 //
190
191 generate if (F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET)
192 begin : ASSUME_INITIAL_RESET
193 always @(*)
194 if (!f_past_valid)
195 assume(!i_axi_reset_n);
196 end else begin : ASSERT_INITIAL_RESET
197 always @(*)
198 if (!f_past_valid)
199 assert(!i_axi_reset_n);
200 end endgenerate
201
202
203 //
204 // If asserted, the reset must be asserted for a minimum of 16 clocks
205 initial f_reset_length = 0;
206 always @(posedge i_clk)
207 if (F_OPT_NO_RESET || i_axi_reset_n)
208 f_reset_length <= 0;
209 else if (!(&f_reset_length))
210 f_reset_length <= f_reset_length + 1'b1;
211
212
213 //
214 // If the reset is not generated within this particular core, then it
215 // can be assumed if F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET is set
216 generate if (F_OPT_ASSUME_RESET && !F_OPT_NO_RESET)
217 begin : ASSUME_RESET
218 always @(posedge i_clk)
219 if ((f_past_valid)&&(!$past(i_axi_reset_n))&&(!$past(&f_reset_length)))
220 assume(!i_axi_reset_n);
221
222 always @(*)
223 if ((f_reset_length > 0)&&(f_reset_length < 4'hf))
224 assume(!i_axi_reset_n);
225
226 end else if (!F_OPT_NO_RESET)
227 begin : ASSERT_RESET
228
229 always @(posedge i_clk)
230 if ((f_past_valid)&&(!$past(i_axi_reset_n))&&(!$past(&f_reset_length)))
231 assert(!i_axi_reset_n);
232
233 always @(*)
234 if ((f_reset_length > 0)&&(f_reset_length < 4'hf))
235 assert(!i_axi_reset_n);
236
237 end endgenerate
238
239 //
240 // All of the xVALID signals *MUST* be set low on the clock following
241 // a reset. Not in the spec, but also checked here is that they must
242 // also be set low initially.
243 always @(posedge i_clk)
244 if ((!f_past_valid && F_OPT_INITIAL)
245 ||(f_past_valid && !$past(i_axi_reset_n)))
246 begin
247 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_arvalid);
248 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_awvalid);
249 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_wvalid);
250 //
251 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_bvalid);
252 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_rvalid);
253 end
254
255 generate if (F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET)
256 begin
257 always @(*)
258 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
259 begin
260 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_arvalid);
261 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_awvalid);
262 `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_wvalid);
263 //
264 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_bvalid);
265 `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_rvalid);
266 end
267 end endgenerate
268 // }}}
269 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
270 //
271 // xRESP checking
272 // {{{
273 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
274
275 always @(*)
276 if ((i_axi_bvalid)&&(!F_OPT_BRESP)&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
277 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bresp == 0);
278 always @(*)
279 if ((i_axi_rvalid)&&(!F_OPT_RRESP)&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
280 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rresp == 0);
281 always @(*)
282 if (i_axi_bvalid&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
283 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bresp != 2'b01); // Exclusive access not allowed
284 always @(*)
285 if (i_axi_rvalid&&(F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
286 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rresp != 2'b01); // Exclusive access not allowed
287
288 // }}}
289 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
290 //
291 // Stability properties--what happens if valid and not ready
292 // {{{
293 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
294 //
295 //
296
297 // Assume any response from the bus will not change prior to that
298 // response being accepted
299 always @(posedge i_clk)
300 if ((f_past_valid)&&($past(i_axi_reset_n))
301 &&(!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
302 begin
303 // Write address channel
304 if ((f_past_valid)&&($past(i_axi_awvalid && !i_axi_awready)))
305 begin
306 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_awvalid);
307 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_awaddr));
308 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_awprot));
309 end
310
311 // Write data channel
312 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
313 &&($past(i_axi_wvalid && !i_axi_wready)))
314 begin
315 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
316 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_wstrb));
317 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_wdata));
318 end
319
320 // Incoming Read address channel
321 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
322 &&($past(i_axi_arvalid && !i_axi_arready)))
323 begin
324 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_arvalid);
325 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_araddr));
326 `SLAVE_ASSUME($stable(i_axi_arprot));
327 end
328
329 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
330 &&($past(i_axi_rvalid && !i_axi_rready)))
331 begin
332 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rvalid);
333 `SLAVE_ASSERT($stable(i_axi_rresp));
334 `SLAVE_ASSERT($stable(i_axi_rdata));
335 end
336
337 if ((f_past_valid && (!F_OPT_ASYNC_RESET || i_axi_reset_n))
338 &&($past(i_axi_bvalid && !i_axi_bready)))
339 begin
340 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bvalid);
341 `SLAVE_ASSERT($stable(i_axi_bresp));
342 end
343 end
344
345 // Nothing should be returned or requested on the first clock
346 generate if (F_OPT_INITIAL)
347 begin : INITIAL_VALUE_CHECKS
348 initial `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_arvalid);
349 initial `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_awvalid);
350 initial `SLAVE_ASSUME(!i_axi_wvalid);
351 //
352 initial `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_bvalid);
353 initial `SLAVE_ASSERT(!i_axi_rvalid);
354 end endgenerate
355 // }}}
356 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
357 //
358 //
359 // Insist upon a maximum delay before a request is accepted
360 //
361 //
362 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
363 //
364 generate if (F_AXI_MAXWAIT > 0)
365 begin : CHECK_STALL_COUNT
366 reg [LGTIMEOUT-1:0] f_axi_awstall,
367 f_axi_wstall,
368 f_axi_arstall;
369
370 //
371 // AXI write address channel
372 //
373 // Count the number of times AWVALID is true while AWREADY
374 // is false. These are stalls, and we want to insist on a
375 // minimum number of them. However, if BVALID && !BREADY,
376 // then there's a reason for not accepting anything more.
377 // Similarly, many cores will only ever accept one request
378 // at a time, hence we won't count things as stalls if
379 // WR-PENDING > 0.
380 initial f_axi_awstall = 0;
381 always @(posedge i_clk)
382 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_awvalid)||(i_axi_awready)
383 ||(i_axi_bvalid))
384 f_axi_awstall <= 0;
385 else if ((f_axi_awr_outstanding >= f_axi_wr_outstanding)
386 &&(i_axi_awvalid && !i_axi_wvalid))
387 // If we are waiting for the write channel to be valid
388 // then don't count stalls
389 f_axi_awstall <= 0;
390 else
391 f_axi_awstall <= f_axi_awstall + 1'b1;
392
393 always @(*)
394 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_awstall < F_AXI_MAXWAIT);
395
396 //
397 // AXI write data channel
398 //
399 // Count the number of clock cycles that the write data
400 // channel is stalled, that is while WVALID && !WREADY.
401 // Since things can back up if BVALID & !BREADY, we avoid
402 // counting clock cycles in that circumstance
403 initial f_axi_wstall = 0;
404 always @(posedge i_clk)
405 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_wvalid)||(i_axi_wready)
406 ||(i_axi_bvalid))
407 f_axi_wstall <= 0;
408 else if ((f_axi_wr_outstanding >= f_axi_awr_outstanding)
409 &&(!i_axi_awvalid && i_axi_wvalid))
410 // If we are waiting for the write address channel
411 // to be valid, then don't count stalls
412 f_axi_wstall <= 0;
413 else
414 f_axi_wstall <= f_axi_wstall + 1'b1;
415
416 always @(*)
417 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wstall < F_AXI_MAXWAIT);
418
419 //
420 // AXI read address channel
421 //
422 // Similar to the first two above, once the master raises
423 // ARVALID, insist that the slave respond within a minimum
424 // number of clock cycles. Exceptions include any time
425 // RVALID is true, since that can back up the whole system,
426 // and any time the number of bursts is greater than zero,
427 // since many slaves can only accept one request at a time.
428 initial f_axi_arstall = 0;
429 always @(posedge i_clk)
430 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_arvalid)||(i_axi_arready)
431 ||(i_axi_rvalid))
432 f_axi_arstall <= 0;
433 else
434 f_axi_arstall <= f_axi_arstall + 1'b1;
435
436 always @(*)
437 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_arstall < F_AXI_MAXWAIT);
438
439 end endgenerate
440
441 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
442 //
443 //
444 // Insist upon a maximum delay before any response is accepted
445 //
446 // These are separate from the earlier ones, in case you wish to
447 // control them separately. For example, an interconnect might be
448 // forced to let a channel wait indefinitely for access, but it might
449 // not be appropriate to require the response to be able to wait
450 // indefinitely as well
451 //
452 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
453 //
454 generate if (F_AXI_MAXRSTALL > 0)
455 begin : CHECK_RESPONSE_STALLS
456 reg [LGTIMEOUT-1:0] f_axi_bstall,
457 f_axi_rstall;
458
459 // AXI write response channel
460 //
461 // Insist on a maximum number of clocks that BVALID can be
462 // high while BREADY is low
463 initial f_axi_bstall = 0;
464 always @(posedge i_clk)
465 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_bvalid)||(i_axi_bready))
466 f_axi_bstall <= 0;
467 else
468 f_axi_bstall <= f_axi_bstall + 1'b1;
469
470 always @(*)
471 `SLAVE_ASSUME(f_axi_bstall < F_AXI_MAXRSTALL);
472
473 // AXI read response channel
474 //
475 // Insist on a maximum number of clocks that RVALID can be
476 // high while RREADY is low
477 initial f_axi_rstall = 0;
478 always @(posedge i_clk)
479 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(!i_axi_rvalid)||(i_axi_rready))
480 f_axi_rstall <= 0;
481 else
482 f_axi_rstall <= f_axi_rstall + 1'b1;
483
484 always @(*)
485 `SLAVE_ASSUME(f_axi_rstall < F_AXI_MAXRSTALL);
486
487 end endgenerate
488
489 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
490 //
491 //
492 // Xilinx extensions/guarantees to the AXI protocol
493 //
494 // 1. The address line will never be more than two clocks ahead of
495 // the write data channel, and
496 // 2. The write data channel will never be more than one clock
497 // ahead of the address channel.
498 //
499 //
500 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
501 //
502 //
503 generate if (F_OPT_XILINX)
504 begin
505 // Rule number one:
506 always @(posedge i_clk)
507 if ((i_axi_reset_n)&&($past(i_axi_reset_n))
508 &&($past(i_axi_awvalid && !i_axi_wvalid,2))
509 &&($past(f_axi_awr_outstanding>=f_axi_wr_outstanding,2))
510 &&(!$past(i_axi_wvalid)))
511 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
512
513 always @(posedge i_clk)
514 if ((i_axi_reset_n)
515 &&(f_axi_awr_outstanding > 1)
516 &&(f_axi_awr_outstanding-1 > f_axi_wr_outstanding))
517 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
518
519 always @(posedge i_clk)
520 if ((i_axi_reset_n)
521 &&($past(f_axi_awr_outstanding > f_axi_wr_outstanding))
522 &&(!$past(axi_wr_req)))
523 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid);
524
525
526 // Rule number two:
527 always @(posedge i_clk)
528 if ((i_axi_reset_n)&&(f_axi_awr_outstanding < f_axi_wr_outstanding))
529 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_awvalid);
530 end endgenerate
531
532 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
533 //
534 //
535 // Count outstanding transactions. With these measures, we count
536 // once per any burst.
537 //
538 //
539 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
540 //
541 //
542
543 //
544 // Count outstanding write address channel requests
545 initial f_axi_awr_outstanding = 0;
546 always @(posedge i_clk)
547 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
548 f_axi_awr_outstanding <= 0;
549 else case({ (axi_awr_req), (axi_wr_ack) })
550 2'b10: f_axi_awr_outstanding <= f_axi_awr_outstanding + 1'b1;
551 2'b01: f_axi_awr_outstanding <= f_axi_awr_outstanding - 1'b1;
552 default: begin end
553 endcase
554
555 //
556 // Count outstanding write data channel requests
557 initial f_axi_wr_outstanding = 0;
558 always @(posedge i_clk)
559 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
560 f_axi_wr_outstanding <= 0;
561 else case({ (axi_wr_req), (axi_wr_ack) })
562 2'b01: f_axi_wr_outstanding <= f_axi_wr_outstanding - 1'b1;
563 2'b10: f_axi_wr_outstanding <= f_axi_wr_outstanding + 1'b1;
564 default: begin end
565 endcase
566
567 //
568 // Count outstanding read requests
569 initial f_axi_rd_outstanding = 0;
570 always @(posedge i_clk)
571 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
572 f_axi_rd_outstanding <= 0;
573 else case({ (axi_ard_req), (axi_rd_ack) })
574 2'b01: f_axi_rd_outstanding <= f_axi_rd_outstanding - 1'b1;
575 2'b10: f_axi_rd_outstanding <= f_axi_rd_outstanding + 1'b1;
576 default: begin end
577 endcase
578
579 //
580 // Do not let the number of outstanding requests overflow
581 always @(posedge i_clk)
582 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wr_outstanding < {(F_LGDEPTH){1'b1}});
583 always @(posedge i_clk)
584 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_awr_outstanding < {(F_LGDEPTH){1'b1}});
585 always @(posedge i_clk)
586 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_rd_outstanding < {(F_LGDEPTH){1'b1}});
587
588 //
589 // That means that requests need to stop when we're almost full
590 always @(posedge i_clk)
591 if ((F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n) && f_axi_awr_outstanding == { {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b1}}, 1'b0} )
592 assert(!i_axi_awvalid);
593 always @(posedge i_clk)
594 if ((F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n) && f_axi_wr_outstanding == { {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b1}}, 1'b0} )
595 assert(!i_axi_wvalid);
596 always @(posedge i_clk)
597 if ((F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n) && f_axi_rd_outstanding == { {(F_LGDEPTH-1){1'b1}}, 1'b0} )
598 assert(!i_axi_arvalid);
599
600 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
601 //
602 //
603 // Insist that all responses are returned in less than a maximum delay
604 // In this case, we count responses within a burst, rather than entire
605 // bursts.
606 //
607 //
608 // A unique feature to the backpressure mechanism within AXI is that
609 // we have to reset our delay counters in the case of any push back,
610 // since the response can't move forward if the master isn't (yet)
611 // ready for it.
612 //
613 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
614 generate if (F_AXI_MAXDELAY > 0)
615 begin : CHECK_MAX_DELAY
616
617 reg [LGTIMEOUT-1:0] f_axi_wr_ack_delay,
618 f_axi_rd_ack_delay;
619
620 //
621 // Count the clock cycles a write request (address + data) has
622 // been outstanding and without any response
623 initial f_axi_wr_ack_delay = 0;
624 always @(posedge i_clk)
625 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(i_axi_bvalid)
626 ||(f_axi_awr_outstanding==0)
627 ||(f_axi_wr_outstanding==0))
628 f_axi_wr_ack_delay <= 0;
629 else if (f_axi_wr_outstanding > 0)
630 f_axi_wr_ack_delay <= f_axi_wr_ack_delay + 1'b1;
631
632 //
633 // Count the clock cycles that any read request has been
634 // outstanding, but without any response.
635 initial f_axi_rd_ack_delay = 0;
636 always @(posedge i_clk)
637 if ((!i_axi_reset_n)||(i_axi_rvalid)||(f_axi_rd_outstanding==0))
638 f_axi_rd_ack_delay <= 0;
639 else
640 f_axi_rd_ack_delay <= f_axi_rd_ack_delay + 1'b1;
641
642
643 //
644 // Assert that write responses will be returned in a timely
645 // fashion
646 always @(*)
647 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wr_ack_delay < F_AXI_MAXDELAY);
648
649 //
650 // Assert that read responses will be returned in a timely
651 // fashion
652 always @(*)
653 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_rd_ack_delay < F_AXI_MAXDELAY);
654
655 end endgenerate
656
657 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
658 //
659 //
660 // Assume acknowledgements must follow requests
661 //
662 // The f_axi*outstanding counters count the number of requests. No
663 // acknowledgment should issue without a pending request
664 // burst. Further, the spec is clear: you can't acknowledge something
665 // on the same clock you get the request. There must be at least one
666 // clock delay.
667 //
668 //
669 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
670
671 //
672 // AXI write response channel
673 //
674 always @(posedge i_clk)
675 if (i_axi_bvalid && (F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
676 begin
677 // No BVALID w/o an outstanding request
678 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_awr_outstanding > 0);
679 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_wr_outstanding > 0);
680 end
681
682 //
683 // AXI read data channel signals
684 //
685 always @(posedge i_clk)
686 if (i_axi_rvalid && (F_OPT_INITIAL || i_axi_reset_n))
687 // No RVALID w/o an outstanding request
688 `SLAVE_ASSERT(f_axi_rd_outstanding > 0);
689
690 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
691 //
692 //
693 // F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY or F_OPT_READ_ONLY
694 //
695 // Optionally disable either read or write channels (or both??)
696 //
697 //
698 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
699 //
700 //
701 initial assert((!F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY)||(!F_OPT_READ_ONLY));
702
703 generate if (F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY)
704 begin : NO_READS
705
706 // If there are no read requests (assumed), there should be
707 // no read responses
708 always @(*)
709 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_arvalid == 0);
710 always @(*)
711 assert(f_axi_rd_outstanding == 0);
712 always @(*)
713 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_rvalid == 0);
714
715 end endgenerate
716
717 generate if (F_OPT_READ_ONLY)
718 begin : NO_WRITES
719
720 // If there are no write requests (assumed, address or data),
721 // there should be no read responses
722 always @(*)
723 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_awvalid == 0);
724 always @(*)
725 `SLAVE_ASSUME(i_axi_wvalid == 0);
726 always @(*)
727 assert(f_axi_wr_outstanding == 0);
728 always @(*)
729 assert(f_axi_awr_outstanding == 0);
730 always @(*)
731 `SLAVE_ASSERT(i_axi_bvalid == 0);
732
733 end endgenerate
734
735 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
736 //
737 //
738 // Cover properties
739 //
740 // We'll use this to prove that transactions are even possible, and
741 // hence that we haven't so constrained the bus that nothing can take
742 // place.
743 //
744 //
745 ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
746
747 //
748 // AXI write response channel
749 //
750 generate if (!F_OPT_READ_ONLY)
751 begin
752 always @(posedge i_clk)
753 // Make sure we can get a write acknowledgment
754 cover((i_axi_bvalid)&&(i_axi_bready));
755 end endgenerate
756
757 //
758 // AXI read response channel
759 //
760 generate if (!F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY)
761 begin
762 always @(posedge i_clk)
763 // Make sure we can get a response from the read channel
764 cover((i_axi_rvalid)&&(i_axi_rready));
765 end endgenerate
766
767 generate if (!F_OPT_READ_ONLY && F_OPT_COVER_BURST > 0)
768 begin : COVER_WRITE_BURSTS
769
770 reg [31:0] cvr_writes;
771
772 initial cvr_writes = 0;
773 always @(posedge i_clk)
774 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
775 cvr_writes <= 0;
776 else if (i_axi_bvalid && i_axi_bready && i_axi_bresp == 2'b00
777 && !(&cvr_writes))
778 cvr_writes <= cvr_writes + 1;
779
780 always @(*)
781 cover(cvr_writes == F_OPT_COVER_BURST);
782
783 end endgenerate
784
785 generate if (!F_OPT_WRITE_ONLY && F_OPT_COVER_BURST > 0)
786 begin : COVER_READ_BURSTS
787
788 reg [31:0] cvr_reads;
789
790 initial cvr_reads = 0;
791 always @(posedge i_clk)
792 if (!i_axi_reset_n)
793 cvr_reads <= 0;
794 else if (i_axi_rvalid && i_axi_rready && i_axi_rresp == 2'b00
795 && !(&cvr_reads))
796 cvr_reads <= cvr_reads + 1;
797
798 always @(*)
799 cover(cvr_reads == F_OPT_COVER_BURST);
800
801 end endgenerate
802
803`undef SLAVE_ASSUME
804`undef SLAVE_ASSERT
805endmodule
